#### R42: `dataplane.appPortsFromSpec` wraps at 65535 and makes a valid DNAT application apply non-terminating

Title: `dataplane.appPortsFromSpec` wraps at 65535 and makes a valid DNAT application apply non-terminating
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1348-1356` parses boundaries as `uint16`, then increments the inferred `uint16` loop variable through its maximum: ```go lo, hi, err := parsePortRange(spec) if err != nil { return nil } if hi > lo { var ports []int for p := lo; p <= hi; p++ { ports = append(ports, int(p)) } ``` `parsePortRange` explicitly returns `(uint16, uint16, error)` at `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1364` and narrows the accepted 16-bit endpoints at line 1378. A live DNAT application reaches the helper at `pkg/dataplane/compiler_nat.go:812-818`: ```go if rule.Match.Application != "" { userApps := cfg.Applications.Applications // Try single application first app, found := config.ResolveApplication(rule.Match.Application, userApps) if found { appTerms = append(appTerms, dnatAppTerm{proto: app.Protocol, ports: appPortsFromSpec(app.DestinationPort)}) } else if _, isSet := cfg.Applications.ApplicationSets[rule.Match.Application]; isSet { ``` The retained shim invokes the shared compiler at `pkg/dataplane/loader.go:181-185`: ```go m.SelectUserspaceXDPShimEntryProgram() compilerDP := userspaceShimCompileDataplane{Manager: m} result, err := CompileConfig(compilerDP, cfg, m.lastCompile != nil) if err != nil { return nil, err } ```
Trace: 1. An operator commits a referenced application such as `protocol tcp; destination-port 1024-65535;` and a destination-NAT rule with `match application <name>`. 2. The strict application gate calls `validatePortSpec`; `pkg/config/compiler_applications.go:1000-1016` accepts ordered endpoints in `1..65535`, and `pkg/config/parser_ast_test.go:5039-5048` explicitly expects `1024-65535` to pass. 3. The serialized daemon apply reaches `userspace.Manager.ApplyConfig -> Manager.Compile -> CompileUserspaceShim -> CompileConfig -> compileNAT`. 4. `parsePortRange` returns `lo=1024`, `hi=65535` as `uint16`. 5. When `p` reaches 65535, `p++` wraps to 0; `p <= hi` remains true. The loop repeatedly appends all 65,536 values and cannot return. 6. The no-op shim `SetDNATEntry` and the Rust snapshot builder are never reached. The apply holds `applySem` while memory grows until cgroup/process OOM or external termination.
Refutation attempt: I checked the strict validator, tolerant representation, helper type, all call sites, adapter behavior, apply cancellation, existing tests, the retirement boundary, and issue history. The parser rejects malformed, reversed, zero-floor, and greater-than-65535 ranges, but it intentionally accepts a lower endpoint below 65535 with a high endpoint exactly 65535. A single port `65535` and an equal range `65535-65535` avoid the loop; any valid ascending range ending at 65535 enters it. `ParseUint(..., 16)` bounds values but leaves the maximum-value increment unsafe. The DNAT adapter's map method is a no-op only after expansion, and the loop has no context/cap check. `TestAppPortsFromSpec` covers `8080-8083` and `443-443` but no maximum endpoint. #1476 did not retire `CompileUserspaceShim`. The candidate therefore survived refutation.
HPC/invariant check: The control-path liveness invariant is that range iteration is monotonic and bounded before a serialized apply publishes state. It fails because a fixed-width unsigned induction variable wraps at its inclusive upper bound. The loop is not on the packet hot path, and atomic ordering, cache-line layout, and endianness are not implicated. It does hold the single apply semaphore and creates unbounded allocation/GC pressure, blocking all other apply producers and HA/config convergence.
Why it matters: A syntactically and semantically valid, persistable config can hang and then OOM `xpfd`. Commit paths persist the active config before dataplane convergence, so restart/boot can replay the same apply and fail repeatedly. A peer-synced configuration can trigger the same path on the standby. The previous Rust snapshot remains authoritative only while the process survives; process death removes control-plane and HA participation and can cause node or cluster availability loss.
Fix direction: Make the induction variable wider than the endpoint (`uint32` or `int`) as the immediate correctness fix, with an overflow-proof termination condition. Prefer eliminating per-port expansion from this compatibility compiler path and carrying a compact `[low, high]` range, especially because shim DNAT writes are no-ops and the live Rust builder already has compact range support. Add a boundary regression for an ascending range ending at 65535 and an end-to-end `CompileUserspaceShim`/DNAT-application test in a subprocess or otherwise bounded harness so a revert cannot OOM the main test process.
Labels: `bug`, `userspace-dataplane`, `nat`, `control-plane`, `integer-overflow`, `resource-exhaustion`, `ha`
Dedup note: Dedup index entries 521 and 641, open cohort #5250, and archived `ps-review-038-A6_go_dataplane_manager-b2`/`ps-review-042` refer to `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat.go::appPortsFromSpec`, where a wider loop terminates after at most 65,535 appends and is then coalesced; their impact is bounded allocation amplification. Closed #3449 fixed compact live DNAT snapshots, and closed #42 covered old per-port application map writes. This finding is the path-qualified `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go` helper, a `uint16` wrap with unbounded append and a non-returning live shim compile. Symbol location, mechanism, and impact are distinct. Fresh GH search found no open issue covering it.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/dataplane/compiler.go:1348`. Independently retained in verify-R37-R48.md at the final target SHA.

#### R46: Orderly HA shutdown relinquishes ownership without stopping the authoritative Kea units

Title: Orderly HA shutdown relinquishes ownership without stopping the authoritative Kea units
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:196-205` removes VRRP ownership and heartbeat without issuing any DHCP-server clear: > 196 `// Stop VRRP manager (removes VIPs, sends priority-0).` > 197 `if d.vrrpMgr != nil {` > 198 `    d.vrrpMgr.Stop()` > 199 `}` > 200 `` > 201 `// Stop cluster monitor (heartbeats) immediately after VRRP priority-0.` > 202 `// This ensures the peer's heartbeat timeout starts promptly instead of` > 203 `// being delayed by the 5s sync Stop timeout below.` > 204 `if d.cluster != nil {` > 205 `    d.cluster.Stop()` The only authoritative demotion clear is `d.dhcpServer.ApplyAsync(nil, ...)` in the VRRP BACKUP callback at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1273-1287`. `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:328-343` explicitly says the stop arm does not emit an event before closing `eventCh`. Kea is external state: `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:126-132,239-253,294-320` owns systemd units and defines `Apply(nil)` as the operation that stops an active unit regardless of which xpfd instance started it.
Trace: Start with this node MASTER for a DHCP-serving RG and Kea active. SIGTERM enters `shutdown`, drains only the current config apply, withdraws RAs/VIPs, sends VRRP priority zero, and stops cluster heartbeat. `vrrpMgr.Stop` intentionally emits no BACKUP event, so `clearRethServicesForRG` never enqueues the nil desired state. xpfd then exits while the independent `kea-dhcp4-server`/`kea-dhcp6-server` systemd unit continues serving the old interfaces. The peer promotes and starts its own Kea generation. Both nodes can answer the same client segment after ownership has transferred.
Refutation attempt: I searched the complete shutdown path and all DHCP references in `daemon_run.go`/`daemon_run_shutdown.go`; there is no synchronous clear, async clear, worker drain, or unit stop. Process exit cannot stop a systemd-managed unit. The manager's generation ordering would make a late synchronous `Apply(nil)` authoritative, but shutdown never calls it. Preserving DHCP client addresses across graceful restart is documented separately and does not justify preserving an HA-gated DHCP server after VRRP relinquishment. This is High rather than Critical because it requires cluster DHCP service plus an orderly stop of an active owner.
HPC/invariant check: Cold lifecycle invariant violated: before an HA node publishes or signals loss of RG ownership, every externally persistent service able to answer for that RG must be synchronously quiesced. Kea must be inactive before priority-zero/heartbeat relinquishment can let the peer serve.
Why it matters: A routine package restart or administrative stop can create persistent dual DHCP, duplicate offers/ACKs, conflicting lease ownership, and client address instability even though VRRP and status correctly show only the peer as owner.
Fix direction: Add a bounded `StopAndDrain`/synchronous newest-generation `Apply(nil)` for cluster Kea before VRRP ownership is relinquished. It must supersede pending MASTER work and report a stop failure through shutdown health/logging. Add RETH and direct-ownership shutdown-order tests proving Kea is inactive before priority zero and that a queued MASTER apply cannot run afterward.
Labels: MATERIAL, daemon-lifecycle, HA, DHCP, Kea, systemd, shutdown-order, dual-service, userspace-live
Dedup note: Open GH #6535 matches `dhcpServer.ApplyAsync` plus lost transition retry debt plus persistent dual DHCP after a failed apply. This finding is a different mechanism at `Daemon.shutdown`/`vrrp.Manager.Stop`: no BACKUP transition and therefore no stop request exists. Closed #1778 made `Apply(nil)` authoritative over stale systemd units, but did not wire that operation into orderly ownership teardown. No symbol+mechanism+impact match exists in the current scratch index or issue history.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1273`. Independently retained in verify-R37-R48.md at the final target SHA.

#### R47: A DHCP lease timer can start a non-cancellable full apply after shutdown's only apply drain

Title: A DHCP lease timer can start a non-cancellable full apply after shutdown's only apply drain
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:49-56` makes background applies wait forever and then run with a fresh non-cancellable context: > 49 `func (d *Daemon) applyConfig(cfg *config.Config) {` > 50 `    _ = d.applySem.Acquire(context.Background(), 1)` > 51 `    defer d.applySem.Release(1)` > 52 `    // Boot / DHCP-callback / feed / config-poll applies must always run to` > 53 `    // completion (they are not request-bound and there is no operator waiting` > 54 `    // to cancel them), so the heavy pipeline is driven with a non-cancellable` > 55 `    // context -- byte-identical to the pre-#2926 behavior.` > 56 `    if err := d.applyConfigLocked(context.Background(), cfg); err != nil {` `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:35-64` cancels and drains `applySem` once, then cancels the run context and waits its `WaitGroup`. DHCP clients are deliberately based on `context.Background()` and survive signal shutdown (`pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:275-280`); their independent `time.AfterFunc` invokes the callback at `:500-512`. `onDHCPAddressChange` can call the full `d.applyConfig(activeCfg)` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:73-114`, and neither the client nor timer belongs to the shutdown wait group.
Trace: A lease update arms the two-second recompile timer. Shutdown cancels the current apply and successfully acquires/releases `applySem`, establishing a false drain point. The timer then fires, reads the still-live active config, acquires `applySem` with `Background`, and starts the full networkd/netlink/FRR/IPsec/dataplane/HA apply. Concurrent shutdown proceeds to fence RGs and stop VRRP, cluster comms, FRR, and the dataplane. The late apply can re-arm state against stopped owners, access managers during teardown, or delay process exit with work shutdown can no longer cancel or join.
Refutation attempt: Canceling the signal/run context does not reach DHCP clients, by explicit design. `applyCancel` does not reach this apply because both semaphore acquisition and `applyConfigLocked` receive new Background contexts. The first semaphore drain covers callbacks already queued ahead of it, not a timer that enters afterward. Process exit eventually kills the goroutine, but only after the race with ordered teardown. GH #6716 is not a defense: it concerns a pre-lock active-config snapshot and still leaves this post-drain lifecycle entry possible.
HPC/invariant check: Cold lifecycle invariant violated: after the apply drain point, no producer may enter `applyConfigLocked`, and every producer that can do so must be quiesced and joined before dependent managers are torn down. Preserving DHCP addresses does not require preserving callback execution.
Why it matters: The shutdown fence is a failover safety boundary. Re-entering the full apply behind it can extend dual ownership, restore state on a demoting node, race external command execution, or dereference service owners after stop.
Fix direction: Give the DHCP manager a `QuiescePreservingLeases` operation that atomically disables/stops the recompile timer, suppresses new callbacks, cancels and joins client workers without deleting installed addresses, and call it before the final apply drain. Also gate every background apply on a daemon generation/context and reject entry after teardown begins. Add a deterministic timer-after-drain test asserting no apply or manager call occurs after the boundary.
Labels: MATERIAL, daemon-lifecycle, DHCP-client, apply-order, shutdown-race, goroutine, timer, netlink, userspace-live
Dedup note: Open GH #6716 matches `onDHCPAddressChange` reading `ActiveConfig` before `applySem`, with stale-snapshot overwrite impact. This finding matches a different mechanism: a Background-owned timer enters after the shutdown drain and races manager teardown. The ip-monitor Background semaphore shutdown issue in checked-in history is also a different producer/stop cycle. No current entry matches this timer+post-drain trace.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:49`. Independently retained in verify-R37-R48.md at the final target SHA.

#### R48: Bootstrap treats a failed lifeline netlink snapshot as DHCP and then cycles the management NIC

Title: Bootstrap treats a failed lifeline netlink snapshot as DHCP and then cycles the management NIC
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:917-924` converts an empty address observation into an authoritative DHCP networkd file: > 917 `// Snapshot the lifeline's addressing ONCE (Copilot: avoid the duplicate` > 918 `// netlink walk). DHCP-managed or address-less lifelines get a plain DHCP` > 919 `// .network; a statically-addressed one gets an Address=/Gateway= snapshot.` > 920 `v4, v6, gw4, gw6 := interfaceAddrSnapshot(lifeline)` > 921 `var content string` > 922 `if isDHCPManaged(lifeline) || (len(v4) == 0 && len(v6) == 0) {` > 923 `    content = "# Managed by xpfd -- #1922 bootstrap lifeline (DHCP)\n" +` > 924 `        "[Match]\nName=fxp0\n\n[Network]\nDHCP=yes\n\n[DHCPv4]\nUseDNS=yes\nUseRoutes=yes\n"` The observation function returns exactly that empty tuple on `LinkByName` failure and discards `AddrList` errors (`pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:974-982`); it also continues past each `RouteList` error (`:993-997`). The caller writes the resulting `.network`, writes `.link`, renames/cycles to `fxp0`, and reloads networkd at `:886-905`.
Trace: A remote operator reaches a cold-boot appliance over a statically addressed enumeration-index-0 management NIC. Lifeline route discovery succeeds, but the later address or route netlink dump transiently fails. `interfaceAddrSnapshot` represents uncertainty as empty data. `writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork` chooses `DHCP=yes` (or omits the static default gateway), after which the caller renames and cycles the only reachable NIC. If the segment has no DHCP server, or if the lost gateway was required, the old static lifeline cannot return under `fxp0` and remote management is lost.
Refutation attempt: The earlier lifeline discovery does not preserve the address/prefix/gateway payload, only interface identity. `isDHCPManaged` is ORed with the empty snapshot condition, so a correctly detected static owner cannot prevent the fallback. Networkd reload cannot reconstruct data never written. The index-0 guard narrows the trigger but this is exactly the NIC the function is willing to cycle. The ignored writer/rename/reload errors were excluded from this finding because GH #5842 already owns that laundering mechanism.
HPC/invariant check: Bootstrap safety invariant violated: management-interface mutation may proceed only from a complete, successful lifeline snapshot. Unknown observation state must be distinct from a valid address-less/DHCP state; no hot-path cost is involved.
Why it matters: A transient netlink read failure during first boot can turn a healthy static management path into an unrecoverable remote lockout precisely while bootstrap is intended to preserve it.
Fix direction: Return a typed snapshot plus error, propagate address and route dump failures, and abort before writing `.network`/`.link` or cycling the link when the observation is incomplete. Distinguish an intentionally empty snapshot from read failure. Add injected LinkByName/AddrList/RouteList failure tests that assert zero file, rename, link-cycle, and reload calls.
Labels: MATERIAL, bootstrap, management-lifeline, netlink, systemd-networkd, cold-boot, remote-lockout, userspace-live

A7-b1-03 is rooted earlier at `interfaceAddrSnapshot`: failed observation is positively misclassified as DHCP or a gateway-free static snapshot, even if all later writes and commands succeed. No current index/history entry names that symbol+mechanism+impact combination.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:917`. Independently retained in verify-R37-R48.md at the final target SHA.

#### R49: Normal apply discards every login, sudoers, deprovision, sshd, and root-auth failure

Title: Normal apply discards every login, sudoers, deprovision, sshd, and root-auth failure
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:97-104` explicitly limits error collection to shutdown closeout: > 97 `// Steps 11-13 are the login/credential reconcilers. They return their` > 98 `// accumulated failures (#5874) so the cancel closeout can surface them,` > 99 `// but on the NORMAL apply path the returns are intentionally DISCARDED:` > 100 `// the tail is best-effort here because the next boot re-renders login /` > 101 `// sudoers / SSH / root-auth from the active config, so a transient failure` > 102 `// converges (the #2926 next-boot contract). Only the daemon-stop cancel` > 103 `// closeout -- where next-boot convergence does NOT happen while the daemon` > 104 `// stays intentionally stopped -- collects and fails on these.` The five calls are assigned to `_` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:106-127`. The final `errors.Join` at `:316-327` includes networkd, dataplane, Kea, nft, IPsec, interface, route-leak, rule, management-route, VRF, and VRRP failures, but none of those credential-owner errors. The closeout owner list at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_hostauth.go:47-62` confirms that each function already returns an actionable error and is considered part of host authorization.
Trace: An operator removes a user, downgrades a class, rotates root authentication, or disables root SSH. The corresponding filesystem ownership, `useradd`/`chpasswd`, sudoers write, authorized-keys revoke, sshd config write, or service reload fails. The function returns an error, but normal apply discards it and the commit reports success. The stale password/key, NOPASSWD grant, or `PermitRootLogin` state remains effective with no retry debt; only an unrelated later apply or reboot may try again.
Refutation attempt: "Next boot" is neither a bounded runtime retry nor acceptable confirmation for a security-revocation commit. The owners run independently, so collecting errors does not require short-circuiting later steps. Existing owner tests prove local failure returns and the shutdown-closeout tests prove aggregation is feasible, but no normal-tail test requires propagation. Closed owner-specific issues fixed reconcile semantics, not this call-site discard.
HPC/invariant check: Security apply invariant violated: a successful commit may be reported only after every owner of host-login authorization either converges or records a surfaced failure/debt. These are cold apply operations; joining their existing errors adds no hot-path cost.
Why it matters: Operators can receive a successful commit while credentials they explicitly revoked remain usable indefinitely. That is a durable privilege-retention failure, not merely delayed cosmetic state.
Fix direction: Run all five owners, collect every returned error, and include them in the tail's final `errors.Join`; keep collect-all ordering so one failure does not suppress later revocations. Record health/retry debt for background applies that have no commit caller. Add injected-failure tests for each owner proving normal commit fails while all later owners still execute.
Labels: MATERIAL, host-integration, authentication, authorization, sudoers, sshd, systemd, apply-error, privilege-retention, userspace-live

A7-b1-04 is the distinct normal-path call-site mechanism at `applyTailReconciles`, where all five results are intentionally discarded and absent from the final join. No exact current issue matches it.

#### R50: Fabric IPVLAN apply converts terminal netlink failures into success and has no persistent recovery owner

Title: Fabric IPVLAN apply converts terminal netlink failures into success and has no persistent recovery owner
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:86-95` logs exhaustion and then returns no error to the apply transaction: > 86 `retryErr = ensureFabricIPVLAN(parentLinux, fabLinux, addrs)` > 87 `if retryErr == nil {` > 88 `    break` > 89 `}` > 90 `}` > 91 `if retryErr != nil {` > 92 `    slog.Error("CRITICAL: fabric IPVLAN creation failed after retries -- cluster heartbeat will not work",` > 93 `        "parent", parentLinux, "name", fabLinux, "err", retryErr)` > 94 `}` > 95 `continue` `applyFabricIPVLAN` is void and its caller cannot add the failure to apply debt. `ensureFabricIPVLAN` also logs and ignores parent-up/MTU, overlay MTU, and configured `AddrReplace` failures before returning nil (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_fabric.go:29-50,72-96`). Fabric session/config sync waits only 30 times for an address and then exits (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:793-812`); heartbeat startup likewise has a terminal 30x2s budget at `:1304-1348`. None of those consumers recreates the overlay.
Trace: On cold boot, parent readiness, device creation, namespace state, or address installation remains unavailable past the fixed apply retry window. A `LinkAdd` failure is logged after six attempts and forgotten; an `AddrReplace` failure is even reported as a successful ensure. The config apply completes successfully. Session/config sync and, where configured on that path, heartbeat resolve no local address, exhaust their independent minute-long waits, and exit permanently. No level-triggered owner retries the desired overlay; only an unrelated config apply or daemon restart can heal it.
Refutation attempt: Networkd can configure an address only after the expected netdev exists and is matched; it cannot recover a permanently absent overlay on behalf of this imperative owner. Consumer retries observe addresses but never call `ensureFabricIPVLAN`. The userspace XSK callback supplies at most another untracked attempt and itself only logs failure. Closed #127 repaired address reconciliation when an existing overlay is observed; it did not propagate failures or establish retry debt. The failure can isolate HA control traffic, so it remains High despite requiring a prolonged/transient cold-boot fault.
HPC/invariant check: Control-plane convergence invariant violated: every configured fabric overlay and address must have one level-triggered owner that retries until success or daemon cancellation, and apply success must mean the required netlink state was observed. Work is cold-path and may be event/timer driven without touching packet processing.
Why it matters: A recoverable boot-order race can become permanent cluster isolation for the lifetime of xpfd. Config/session sync disappears, heartbeat may disappear, and ownership safety can degrade or split while the active configuration is reported as applied.
Fix direction: Make `ensureFabricIPVLAN` return all link/MTU/address/up failures and make `applyFabricIPVLAN` return an aggregate error into the apply tail. Add a daemon-context, generation-fenced reconciliation loop driven by link events plus bounded backoff that continues until the overlay and addresses are observed. Consumers should depend on readiness rather than carry their own terminal retry budgets. Test transient LinkAdd and AddrReplace failures followed by recovery without another commit.
Labels: MATERIAL, HA, fabric, IPVLAN, netlink, cold-boot, retry-debt, session-sync, heartbeat, userspace-live
Dedup note: `claude-review-002` matches `applyFabricIPVLAN` sleeping five seconds while holding `applySem`, with commit/config-sync latency impact. `gemini-review-042` matches the disabled `continue` and loss of AF_XDP zero-copy. Closed #127 matches omission of address reconciliation on an already-existing overlay. A7-b1-05 instead matches swallowed terminal netlink outcomes plus the absence of a persistent owner, causing reported convergence and long-lived HA isolation.

#### R55: FRR non-protocol route rendering lacks a final operand-validity belt

Title: FRR non-protocol route rendering lacks a final operand-validity belt
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:165-169` accepts a generate-route destination without a key validator: ```go 165 "generate": {desc: "Generated routes", children: map[string]*schemaNode{ 166     "route": {desc: "Generated route", args: 1, placeholder: "<destination>", children: map[string]*schemaNode{ 167         "policy":  {desc: "Policy", args: 1, placeholder: "<policy>", children: nil}, 168         "discard": {desc: "Discard route", children: nil}, 169     }}, ``` `pkg/frr/config_render.go:245-254` classifies the raw string by colon and emits it directly: ```go 245 func renderGenerateRoutes(b *strings.Builder, fc *FullConfig) { 246     if len(fc.GenerateRoutes) == 0 { 247         return 248     } 249     for _, gr := range fc.GenerateRoutes { 250         if strings.Contains(gr.Prefix, ":") { 251             fmt.Fprintf(b, "ipv6 route %s blackhole\n", gr.Prefix) 252         } else { 253             fmt.Fprintf(b, "ip route %s blackhole\n", gr.Prefix) 254         } ``` The backup-router validator explicitly downgrades malformed input on tolerant load, promising omission at `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:2531-2539`: ```go 2531 if net.ParseIP(nh) == nil { 2532     msg := fmt.Sprintf( 2533         "system backup-router %s: not a valid IP address; FRR rejects a "+ 2534             "malformed next-hop, which fails the entire static config "+ 2535             "load (frr-reload)", nh) 2536     if !lenient { 2537         return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", msg) 2538     } 2539     warnings = append(warnings, msg+" (ignored: backup-router default route not installed until corrected)") ``` The renderer does not implement that promise at `pkg/frr/config_render.go:365-370`: ```go 365 prefix := "ip" 366 if nhV6 || strings.Contains(dst, ":") { 367     prefix = "ipv6" 368 } 369 fmt.Fprintf(b, "%s route %s %s 250\n", prefix, dst, fc.BackupRouter) 370 b.WriteString("!\n") ``` The same mechanism affects leniently retained static routes: `generateStaticRouteInTable` uses `sr.Destination`, `nh.Address`, and `nh.Interface` directly at `pkg/frr/config_render.go:123-236`; `compiler_validate_warn.go:646-657` warns about malformed static destinations but does not remove them.
Trace: (1) An operator can commit `routing-options generate route "not a prefix"` because the schema declares one argument but no destination validator. Alternatively, an older persisted or HA-synced malformed static/backup route is retained by the tolerant compiler. (2) `assembleFRRConfig` copies those typed values into `FullConfig`. (3) `renderGenerateRoutes`, `generateStaticRouteInTable`, or `renderBackupRouter` writes the raw operand into the managed section. (4) `frr-reload.py` feeds the section to vtysh as one reload; an invalid static command returns non-zero. (5) The new managed FRR configuration does not converge, affecting valid routes and protocols that shared the reload.
Refutation attempt: I checked the static-route key validators, strict backup-router checks, tolerant warning pass, full-config assembler, global control-character walk, and FRR render validators. Strict static/backup commits are protected, but those errors are intentionally warnings on boot/HA sync; generate-route has no strict destination validator at all. Control-character sanitization prevents multiline injection, not malformed CIDR/IP/interface operands. No renderer-side predicate omits these route objects, and assigned tests cover valid generate/backup/static output only.
HPC/invariant check: This is outside the packet hot path. The violated convergence invariant is that tolerant boot/HA input may warn and omit an unsafe object but must not poison the shared FRR reload or publish runtime convergence before success.
Why it matters: One malformed generated or leniently retained route can prevent all valid FRR changes from loading at cold boot or after HA sync, leaving routing unavailable or stale rather than isolating the bad route as the warning promises.
Fix direction: Add `ValidateRouteDestination` (or a generate-specific CIDR validator) to the generate-route identity. Add shared render-side validators for static destination/next-hop/interface and backup destination/next-hop; on tolerant input, log and omit only the invalid route. Add strict generate rejection plus lenient-load/HA-sync tests that assert valid sibling routes still reload.
Labels: bug, frr, routing, cold-boot, ha-sync, convergence, vsrx-parity
Dedup note: Distinct from closed #2891/#2911/#4808, which added backup family/strict validation but not tolerant render omission, and from closed #4097, which covered multiline community/as-path values. Symbol, mechanism, and whole-reload impact searches found no current open issue for non-protocol route operand omission.

#### R56: BGP neighbor identity can span multiple FRR tokens and is reused raw by BGP and BFD

Title: BGP neighbor identity can span multiple FRR tokens and is reused raw by BGP and BFD
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: The neighbor identity has no key validator at `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:402-407`: ```go 402 "neighbor": {desc: "BGP neighbor", args: 1, placeholder: "<address>", children: map[string]*schemaNode{ 403     "description":            {desc: "Description", args: 1, scalar: true, placeholder: "<text>", children: nil}, 404     "peer-as":                {desc: "Peer AS number", args: 1, valueType: ValueInteger, placeholder: "<as-number>", validator: ValidateInteger(1, 4294967295), children: nil}, 405     "local-as":               {desc: "Local AS number for this peering", args: 1, valueType: ValueInteger, placeholder: "<as-number>", validator: ValidateInteger(1, 4294967295), children: nil}, 406     "local-address":          {desc: "Local address (BGP update-source)", args: 1, placeholder: "<address>", children: nil}, 407     "hold-time":              {desc: "Hold time (seconds)", args: 1, valueType: ValueInteger, placeholder: "<seconds>", validator: ValidateBGPHoldTime, children: nil}, ``` The shared render filter at `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:237-245` checks only `PeerAS`: ```go 237 var validNeighbors []*config.BGPNeighbor 238 if bgp != nil { 239     validNeighbors = make([]*config.BGPNeighbor, 0, len(bgp.Neighbors)) 240     for _, n := range bgp.Neighbors { 241         if n.PeerAS == 0 { 242             continue 243         } 244         validNeighbors = append(validNeighbors, n) 245     } ``` The same raw identity reaches global BFD at `pkg/frr/bfd.go:85-93`: ```go 85 if p.vrfName != "" { 86     // Render belt (#5557): sanitize the routing-instance name like the 87     // `router ... vrf` and static-route vrf clauses. A leniently-loaded 88     // control character in the instance name would otherwise inject a 89     // standalone line into the managed `bfd` block. 90     fmt.Fprintf(&b, " peer %s vrf %s\n", p.address, sanitizeFRRValue(p.vrfName)) 91 } else { 92     fmt.Fprintf(&b, " peer %s\n", p.address) 93 } ``` Every BGP neighbor directive likewise formats `n.Address` raw, beginning at `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:291-317`.
Trace: (1) A quoted neighbor identity containing ordinary ASCII whitespace passes schema validation and the global C0/DEL guard. (2) Compilation retains the complete string with a non-zero peer AS. (3) `validNeighbors` admits it. (4) BGP declaration, activation, route-map, password/BFD directives, and the global BFD peer split the identity into multiple FRR lexer tokens. (5) The resulting commands are rejected or interpreted with different line-local grammar, causing the shared managed reload to fail for otherwise valid peers.
Refutation attempt: I checked schema key validators, compiler BGP gates, `validNeighbors`, `sanitizeFRRValue`, `frrTokenUnsafeIndex`, the #4588 status-query IP guard, and all neighbor/BFD interpolation sites. The global guard rejects C0/DEL and therefore blocks newline command injection, but deliberately preserves space. `frrTokenUnsafeIndex` is used for whitespace-split authentication values, not neighbor identities. #4588 protects read commands only. Peer-AS validation does not constrain the address token.
HPC/invariant check: No packet-path or cache-line concern applies. The violated parser-boundary invariant is that a value occupying one FRR token must be validated as exactly one token before every interpolation site shares it.
Why it matters: A single malformed neighbor can reject a whole FRR reload, taking unrelated BGP peers and routing changes out of convergence; BFD configuration is poisoned by the same identity.
Fix direction: Define one neighbor-identity validator shared by schema/compiler and renderer. Accept the intended set (bare IP, and only explicitly supported hostname/interface/peer-group forms) while rejecting whitespace and FRR token metacharacters. Filter `validNeighbors` with the same predicate so every BGP and BFD loop agrees, and add strict plus lenient-render tests.
Labels: bug, frr, bgp, bfd, input-validation, ha-sync, convergence
Dedup note: Distinct from closed #4588 (untrusted show-query command input), closed #4097 (community/as-path multiline values), and GH#6590 (peer-advertised status hostname). No dedup entry covers configured neighbor identity token shape across BGP/BFD rendering.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:402`. Independently retained in opus-verify-R49-R60.md at the final target SHA.

#### R57: Marker-first credential ownership can overclaim pre-existing credentials after a failed mutation

Title: Marker-first credential ownership can overclaim pre-existing credentials after a failed mutation
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: Key ownership is durably claimed before any directory/chown/content mutation at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1176-1185`: ```go 1176 // #5841 marker-first: record SSH-KEY ownership BEFORE writing 1177 // authorized_keys. This is a DISTINCT marker from the 1178 // password/account markers, so setting only a password never claims 1179 // the key file — the emptied-key / deprovision reconcilers only 1180 // remove a key file this marker proves xpf wrote. Written 1181 // unconditionally (idempotent) so an upgrade that already has 1182 // xpf-written keys but no key marker gains one on the next apply. 1183 // Fail VISIBLE: if the durable marker cannot be written, skip the 1184 // key write and retry next apply rather than leave a 1185 // written-but-unmarked key grant (the underclaim). ``` The following durable write can fail without rolling that newly created marker back at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1231-1236`: ```go 1231 if err := fsatomic.WriteFileDurable(keysFile, []byte(keysContent), 0600, fsatomic.WithOwner(uid, gid)); err != nil { 1232     slog.Warn("failed to write authorized_keys", 1233         "user", user.Name, "err", err) 1234     fail(fmt.Errorf("write authorized_keys for %s: %w", user.Name, err)) 1235     continue 1236 } ``` Password and root-key paths have the same ordering at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1457-1487` and `1823-1863`. Later removal trusts `passwordProvisioned`/`keyProvisioned` and locks or removes the resource (`1240-1270`, `1494-1507`, and `login_password.go:507-556`).
Trace: (1) A pre-existing account has an operator-managed password or `authorized_keys`. (2) Config asks xpf to replace that resource. (3) xpf writes a durable ownership marker. (4) `chpasswd`, mkdir/chown, or `WriteFileDurable` fails, or power is lost in that interval, so the pre-existing credential remains unchanged. (5) Before a successful retry, config removes the credential/user. (6) Revoke sees the marker as proof xpf created the still-pre-existing resource and locks the password or deletes the key file.
Refutation attempt: I checked resource-specific UID markers, marker-write failure tests, retry behavior, deprovision scoping, root parity, and crash durability. Resource-specific markers solve cross-resource and UID-reuse errors, and marker-first prevents the older underclaim. They do not distinguish a newly recorded intent from a successfully mutated resource. No failure branch removes only a newly created marker; no pending/committed phase exists. The assigned #5841 test injects marker-write failure, not mutation failure after marker success.
HPC/invariant check: This is durable ownership state, not a hot path. The violated crash invariant is two-phase ownership: destructive cleanup may rely only on a committed marker proving the mutation completed, while retry intent must survive separately.
Why it matters: A transient command/filesystem failure or power cut can turn an operator-owned login credential into an xpf-owned one and later delete or lock it, causing administrative lockout and crossing the intended ownership boundary.
Fix direction: Introduce crash-recoverable pending and committed ownership states. Record pending intent before mutation; promote to committed only after success. On failure, remove a newly created pending marker while preserving any pre-existing committed marker. Revocation must trust committed state only. Add password, user-key, and root-key tests for mutation failure, crash-state recovery, config removal before retry, and already-owned retries.
Labels: bug, security, host-auth, lifecycle, durability, cold-boot
Dedup note: This is the inverse residual of closed #5841: that issue fixed mutated-but-unmarked underclaim and cross-resource ownership. The current mechanism is marked-but-not-mutated overclaim with destructive cleanup. No current open issue or prior review entry matched this symbol/mechanism/impact tuple.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1176`. Independently retained in opus-verify-R49-R60.md at the final target SHA.

#### R58: Credential revocation treats unreadable ownership inventories as empty or unowned

Title: Credential revocation treats unreadable ownership inventories as empty or unowned
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: Every marker read error, including `EACCES`, `EIO`, and `ENOTDIR`, is collapsed to “not owned” at `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:265-270`: ```go 265 func hasProvenanceMarker(dir, name string, curUID int) bool { 266     path := markerPathIn(dir, name) 267     data, err := os.ReadFile(path) 268     if err != nil { 269         return false 270     } ``` Every ownership-root enumeration error is likewise ignored at `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:361-367`: ```go 361 func provisionedNames() map[string]struct{} { 362     out := make(map[string]struct{}) 363     for _, dir := range []string{provisionedUsersDir, provisionedPasswordsDir(), provisionedKeysDir()} { 364         entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir) 365         if err != nil { 366             continue // absent/unreadable root contributes no names 367         } ``` The sudoers revocation inventory independently drops its read error at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1357-1364`: ```go 1357 // Revoke: remove any xpf-managed drop-in that is no longer desired. 1358 entries, _ := os.ReadDir(sudoersDir) 1359 for _, e := range entries { 1360     name := e.Name() 1361     if e.IsDir() || !strings.HasPrefix(name, sudoersPrefix) { 1362         continue // leave non-xpf sudoers.d files (and subdirs) alone 1363     } 1364     if _, keep := desired[name]; keep { ``` `reconcileAbsentLoginUsers` returns success immediately for the resulting empty set at `pkg/daemon/login_password.go:433-439`, including during the bounded #5874 cancellation closeout.
Trace: (1) Config removes a managed super-user or root/login credential. (2) The marker directory, individual marker, or sudoers directory returns a transient non-ENOENT read error. (3) Enumeration contributes no name, or ownership checks return false. (4) Password lock, key removal, and/or sudo grant removal are skipped. (5) The reconcile returns nil, so closeout can report convergence and shutdown/promotion can proceed. (6) The removed user's existing host access remains live until some later successful apply happens to revisit it.
Refutation attempt: I compared the marker paths with the `/etc/passwd` and shadow failure handling introduced by #5493, the #5874 closeout callers, and marker cleanup semantics. `lookupUIDErr` correctly distinguishes unreadable from absent and returns retry debt; these marker and directory APIs do not. ENOENT is a valid “absent” result, but the current boolean/map contracts cannot distinguish it from I/O or permission failure. A future ordinary apply may retry, but there is no guarantee of one before shutdown/failover, and current convergence is falsely reported.
HPC/invariant check: No hot-path concern applies. The violated authorization invariant is monotonic revocation: unknown ownership inventory state must retain debt and prevent a successful closeout; only proven absence may release ownership work.
Why it matters: A removed administrator can retain password, SSH-key, or passwordless-sudo access through shutdown or HA transition despite a successful-looking host-auth closeout.
Fix direction: Change marker lookups and inventory enumeration to return `(value, error)`/tri-state. Treat only `ENOENT` as absence, propagate other read errors through `reconcileAbsentLoginUsers`, `deprovisionLoginUser`, root reconciliation, and `reconcileSudoers`, and retain markers/debt. Add injected `ReadDir` and `ReadFile` failures to normal apply and cancellation-closeout tests.
Labels: bug, security, host-auth, teardown, retry-debt, ha
Dedup note: Closed #5493 fixed unreadable `/etc/passwd`, not ownership marker/sudoers inventories. Closed #5874 made returned revocation failures visible, but these read failures currently produce nil. No current issue matches this read-error-collapse mechanism.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1357`. Independently retained in opus-verify-R49-R60.md at the final target SHA.

#### R60: Periodic RG reconciliation can apply an epoch-stale state and temporarily erase retry debt

Title: Periodic RG reconciliation can apply an epoch-stale state and temporarily erase retry debt
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: The assigned state machine has an epoch-aware API, but `MarkApplied` neither takes an epoch nor sets debt when the applied value differs from current desired state (`pkg/daemon/rg_state.go:163-171`): ```go 163 func (s *rgStateMachine) MarkApplied(active bool) { 164     s.mu.Lock() 165     defer s.mu.Unlock() 166     s.applied = active 167     if s.applied == s.active { 168         s.applyPending = false 169     } 170     s.lastRetryLogged = false 171     s.lastApplyErrMsg = "" ``` The narrow caller contract in `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:823-832` performs the external userspace-dataplane side effect and then uses that non-epoch API: ```go 823 if tr.Active { 824     // Activation ordering: set rg_active FIRST, then 825     // remove blackholes. 826     if err := d.dp.HA().SetRGActive(context.Background(), rgID, true); err != nil { 827         if s.ShouldLogApplyError(err.Error()) { 828             slog.Warn("reconcile: failed to update rg_active", 829                 "rg", rgID, "active", true, "err", err) 830         } 831     } else { 832         s.MarkApplied(true) ``` It then applies blackhole state from the same stale transition at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:854-861`: ```go 854 // Declarative blackhole route reconciliation: assert the route 855 // set that should exist regardless of prior transition results. 856 // Active RGs should NOT have blackholes; inactive RGs SHOULD. 857 if tr.Active { 858     d.removeBlackholeRoutes(rgID) 859 } else { 860     d.injectBlackholeRoutes(rgID) 861 } ``` The periodic loop runs every two seconds (`daemon_ha.go:604-619`); `triggerReconcile` exists but has no production callers. Event handlers use `ApplyIfCurrent` via `recordRGActiveAppliedIfCurrentOrStable`, so they do not serialize this periodic writer.
Trace: (1) Periodic reconcile captures `tr.Active=true` at epoch N and starts `SetRGActive(true)`. (2) Before it returns, a cluster/VRRP event advances to epoch N+1, applies `false`, and `ApplyIfCurrent` clears debt because applied now equals desired. (3) The older periodic RPC returns last and sets live `rg_active=true`. (4) `MarkApplied(true)` overwrites `applied`; since desired is false, it does not clear debt, but it also does not restore the debt just cleared in step 2. (5) The stale transition removes blackholes. (6) The node can forward as active until the next two-second sweep recomputes `active != applied` and repairs both effects.
Refutation attempt: I read all state-machine locking/epoch methods, event-handler completion logic, periodic-loop serialization, shutdown join, blackhole ordering, and current open HA issues. The mutex prevents data races but not stale external effects. Event handlers correctly use `ApplyIfCurrent`; the periodic path does not. A subsequent sweep self-heals, but no immediate trigger is wired and a two-second stale-active interval is enough to violate single-owner forwarding. GH#6530 is a separate peer-fence write with persistent blind debt.
HPC/invariant check: Atomic/cache-line concerns do not apply; calls are control-plane RPCs. The violated concurrency invariant is generation monotonicity: an external effect may be acknowledged and followed by dependent blackhole changes only if its captured epoch is still current; any stale completion must reassert debt immediately.
Why it matters: During failover, the old node can re-enter active forwarding and remove its blackholes after a newer demotion, creating a transient dual-active window, duplicate delivery/asymmetric state, and session divergence.
Fix direction: Route periodic completion through `ApplyIfCurrent(tr)` and skip dependent blackhole/readiness effects when stale. Better, re-read `(desired, epoch)` before the external call and retry a changed epoch in the same pass. Make `MarkApplied` set `applyPending = (applied != active)` defensively. Add a deterministic blocked-RPC interleaving test proving a newer demotion cannot be overwritten and no stale blackhole removal occurs.
Labels: bug, ha, race, vrrp, userspace-dataplane, failover
Dedup note: Closed #66 fixed stale cluster/VRRP event handlers; this is the residual periodic writer that still bypasses the epoch API. GH#6530 concerns peer-fence state not being recorded and a persistent blackhole, not a stale periodic completion. No current duplicate matched this interleaving.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:823`. Independently retained in opus-verify-R49-R60.md at the final target SHA.

#### R65: Kernel lo0 mirror omits valid flexible-match-range and widens accepted terms

Title: Kernel lo0 mirror omits valid flexible-match-range and widens accepted terms
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: The assigned netlink schema promises a verbatim copy of every other term field, but has no `FlexMatch` field: `pkg/nftables/netlink_spec.go:71` ```go 71 // Lo0FilterTerm mirrors one lowered config.FirewallFilterTerm for the kernel lo0 72 // input chain. Source/destination scopes are the RESOLVED (prefix-list-expanded) 73 // address lists exactly as dpuserspace.ResolveFilterPrefixListAddrs returns them 74 // — mixed-family and unfiltered; the netlink builder family-filters per chain 75 // pass (mirroring nftFamilyAddrs) and applies the Junos empty-set / except / 76 // match-nothing semantics (mirroring nftAddrPredicate). Every other field is a 77 // verbatim copy of the config term; the builder re-derives protocol numbers, 78 // DSCP values, and tcp-flags masks via the shared SSOT. ``` `pkg/nftables/netlink_spec.go:89` ```go 89 Protocols         []string 90 SourcePorts       []string 91 DestinationPorts  []string 92 SourcePortsExcept []string 93 DestPortsExcept   []string 94 DSCPs             []string 95 ICMPTypes         []int 96 ICMPCodes         []int 97 TCPFlags          []string 98 IsFragment        bool ``` The narrow caller contract confirms that the complete conversion tail copies all other match fields and never copies `term.FlexMatch` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:207-222`, outside assigned scope). The text oracle `nftRulesFromTerm` also has no FlexMatch branch.
Trace: A strict-valid lo0 firewall term carries `config.FirewallFilterTerm.FlexMatch` -> `toNftLo0Term` constructs a schema with no corresponding field -> `buildLo0TermNetlink.applyMatches` cannot emit a payload comparison -> the configured terminating `accept` is emitted with every other predicate but without the byte-range constraint -> ordinary firewall-local traffic is shunted to Linux and evaluated by `inet xpf_lo0`, documented as the primary lo0 enforcement path. The temporary expected-RED test produced: `valid flexible-match-range was dropped; both rules are "accept"`.
Refutation attempt: I checked the strict gates, userspace snapshot builder, lo0 mirror warnings, host-inbound ordering, and both text/netlink renderers. A valid single range with layer-3 or layer-4 start is accepted and enforced by userspace; it is not an unknown/malformed tolerant-path artifact. No commit warning identifies the kernel omission. The later coarse host-inbound chain is not equivalent: a service admitted there can still require the finer lo0 byte match. No later kernel rule restores the missing predicate.
HPC/invariant check: Flex matching is already cache-sensitive in userspace and bounded to one 1-4 byte comparison per term. Adding one nft payload/bitwise/compare expression preserves linear term construction and constant per-rule packet work; it does not introduce an allocation or loop in the userspace hot path. The invariant is that every strict-valid lo0 match either has an equivalent kernel predicate or prevents permissive installation.
Why it matters: A valid vSRX-style RE protection term can be materially broader on the actual host-bound path than configured. An accept term intended for one payload/header pattern becomes an unconditional accept within its remaining scope, exposing control-plane services; a discard term can over-drop. Commit succeeds without a warning.
Fix direction: Add a FlexMatch representation to `Lo0FilterTerm` and copy it in the daemon converter. Lower layer-3/layer-4 starts with nft network/transport payload bases, bounded length, mask, and compare expressions in both the netlink path and parity oracle. If exact support cannot be provided, reject attachment of such a filter to lo0 (or emit a scoped fail-closed rule) rather than omit the predicate. Add strict-valid layer-3/layer-4 mutation, canonical, and privileged-kernel tests.
Labels: `security`, `firewall`, `nftables`, `control-plane`, `fail-open`, `vsrx-parity`, `userspace-live`
Dedup note: No match in `dedup-index.tsv`. Closed #3077 fixed the userspace snapshot omission, while #3203/#3232 cover FlexMatch parsing/start semantics; this finding is the still-live primary kernel lo0 mirror. It is also distinct from current GH#6512, which is limited to partially malformed address lists.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:207`. Independently retained in opus-verify-R61-R73.md at the final target SHA.

#### R66: First apply leaves list-only tunnel members outside their routing-instance VRF

Title: First apply leaves list-only tunnel members outside their routing-instance VRF
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: Once a tunnel has only routing-instance interface-list intent, the post-create tunnel reconcile observes an existing bind and returns; it never performs the bind: `pkg/routing/tunnel.go:1118` ```go 1118 } 1119 if tc.RIListMember != "" { 1120     // Unbind VETO: a stanza→list move must never strip the 0a 1121     // bind (r4 convergent counterexample). 1122     t.observeListClaimLocked(tc, link) 1123     return 1124 } ``` The assigned regression test encodes the missing-first-bind state: `pkg/routing/tunnel_reconcile_test.go:1243` ```go 1243 func TestTunnelVRFListVetoWithFailedBindNoClaim(t *testing.T) { 1244     ops := newFakeLinkOps() 1245     seedVRF(ops, "blue", 200) 1246     tm, _ := newReconcileManager(ops) 1247 1248     // List member configured but 0a's bind failed (master 0) and there 1249     // is no prior claim ⇒ no claim may be invented (r6 Codex). 1250     tc := anchorTC("gr-0-0-0") 1251     tc.RIListMember = "blue" 1252     if err := tm.Apply([]*config.TunnelConfig{tc}); err != nil { ```
Trace: On cold/first apply, daemon step 0a walks `routing-instances ... interface gr-...` before tunnel creation; `BindInterfaceToVRF` returns not-found and is warning-only by design (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:224-236`, narrow contract). `collectAppliedTunnels` then sets `RIListMember`, `ApplyTunnels` creates the link, and the quoted branch only calls `observeListClaimLocked`. Its `MasterIndex == 0` path returns without binding. The temporary expected-RED test observed `first apply master index = 0, want vrf-blue index 200`. In a privileged netns, an address on the unbound link installed `10.0.0.0/30` in `main`; enslaving the link to table-100 `vrf-blue` removed it from `main` and installed it in table 100.
Refutation attempt: I searched for a post-tunnel list bind, networkd `VRF=` generation for arbitrary tunnel RIs, a periodic tunnel apply, and a link-event-triggered full apply. None exists. A second unrelated config/DHCP full apply can make step 0a succeed, and a direct per-tunnel `routing-instance` stanza binds in `reconcileVRFClaimLocked`; those narrow the finding specifically to list-only membership on first/cold creation. A quiet boot can remain unbound indefinitely.
HPC/invariant check: The desired correction is one bounded netlink bind per list-member tunnel during an already serialized tunnel apply. It preserves the claim invariant by recording `appliedRI` only after successful bind or verified master observation. No packet hot-path work or unbounded scan is added.
Why it matters: The tunnel's connected routes and kernel traffic remain in the default routing table instead of the configured virtual-router table. This is a deterministic cold-boot/day-1 VRF isolation breach and route leak on the live userspace anchor path, potentially admitting or exporting traffic in the wrong routing instance until another full apply happens.
Fix direction: After tunnel creation, treat nonempty `RIListMember` as authoritative desired state: if the observed master is not the named VRF, call `BindInterfaceToVRF`, verify/record the claim only on success, and return the genuine post-create failure into commit truth. Preserve direct-stanza precedence and the identity-gated unbind rules. Add a first-apply test that starts with no tunnel link and asserts both `MasterIndex` and connected-route table.

#### R73: Lenient source-NAT aggregate validation still eagerly allocates over-budget bitmap state

Title: Lenient source-NAT aggregate validation still eagerly allocates over-budget bitmap state
Severity: High
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `pkg/config/compiler_nat_source_pool_aggregate_5877_test.go:139-181` proves that three full-range `/16` pools exceed the `2^33` strict slot budget while lenient compilation is warning-only. The downgrade remains explicit at `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_nat.go:228-234`:

```go
if err := validateSourceNATAggregateCardinalityStrict(cfg); err != nil {
    if opts.lenientDestNATAddresses {
        cfg.Warnings = append(cfg.Warnings,
            fmt.Sprintf("source-nat aggregate pool cardinality (downgraded to warning on tolerant path): %v", err))
    } else {
        return err
    }
}
```

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:177-209` emits the addresses without an aggregate-unusable marker. Rust then allocates before reuse at `userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:723-735`:

```rust
if total_pool > 0 {
    rule.pool_allocator = PortAllocator::new(total_pool, port_low, port_high);
}
if let Some(key) = rule.allocator_key() {
    if let Some(existing) = pool_allocators.get(&key) {
        rule.pool_allocator = existing.clone();
    } else {
        let allocator = previous_allocators.get(&key).cloned()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| rule.pool_allocator.clone());
```

Finally, `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:771-790` constructs one occupancy object per address, and `AddressOccupancy::new` at lines 521-535 fills one `Vec<AtomicU64>` word array per port range.
Trace: A pre-gate persisted config or accepted mixed-version peer snapshot reaches `Store.compileTreeLenient`, records only a warning, emits three distinct `/16` pools with the default 64,512-port range, and reaches Rust apply. Rust expands 196,608 addresses and constructs the per-address allocators before reuse. The occupancy words alone represent 12,683,575,296 bits, or 1,585,446,912 bytes (1.476562 GiB), before address vectors, counters, allocator structs, and live-state indexes.
Refutation attempt: Strict operator commit and `ValidatePeerEffectiveSourceNATStrict` reject the shape, but passive Store.Load and tolerant peer ingestion intentionally bypass the hard gate. No Go snapshot poison marks the aggregate unusable, the Rust boundary has only a per-member 65,536-host cap, and `total_pool > 0` allocates even when other failure state exists. Allocator reuse is consulted only after the new allocator has already been built.
HPC/invariant check: The Go cardinality arithmetic saturates correctly and the 1.476562 GiB bitmap calculation is exact. The violated invariant is that compatibility ingestion must remain bounded at the final allocation boundary and preserve last-good service rather than materialize an operator-known over-budget state.
Why it matters: Upgrade boot or HA convergence can stall or OOM the userspace dataplane while processing the legacy configuration that the tolerant path is intended to recover, causing forwarding loss and potentially asymmetric cluster state.
Fix direction: Preflight compact pool/range cardinality in Rust before expansion and allocator construction, reject the apply without replacing last-good state, and make the Go tolerant snapshot omit or poison affected allocator inputs while retaining an actionable warning. Add Go snapshot and Rust apply tests proving that over-budget tolerated input performs no large allocation and preserves prior live state.
Labels: `config`, `source-nat`, `userspace-dp`, `ha`, `resource-exhaustion`, `fail-closed`, `no-brick`

#### R01: Per-session close deletes a shared reverse-NAT steering key

Title: Per-session close deletes a shared reverse-NAT steering key
Severity: Medium
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:198` derives the BPF key from only protocol, translated address, and translated port. It contains neither the original endpoint nor the remote endpoint: ```rust let snat_v4 = match (key.addr_family as i32, nat.rewrite_src?) { (libc::AF_INET, IpAddr::V4(snat_v4)) => snat_v4, _ => return None, }; let snat_port = nat.rewrite_src_port.unwrap_or(key.src_port); let mut dk = [0u8; 12]; dk[0] = key.protocol; dk[4..8].copy_from_slice(&snat_v4.octets()); // #2406: KEY port is HOST-ORDER numeric serialized natively to ``` `userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:1247` confirms live interface SNAT changes only the address and leaves `rewrite_src_port` at its default `None`, so independent flows retaining the same source port can share that key: ```rust return SourceNatLookup::Matched(NatDecision { rewrite_src: Some(rewrite_src), rewrite_dst: None, ..NatDecision::default() }); ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:338` overwrites an existing same-key marker rather than acquiring distinguishable ownership: ```rust let rc = unsafe { libbpf_sys::bpf_map_update_elem( fd, dk.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>(), dv.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>(), libbpf_sys::BPF_ANY as u64, ) ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:259` then unconditionally deletes that shared key. There is no holder count, value/flag check, or compare-before-delete: ```rust // #2979: count the attempt so the close-handler wiring is testable // without a real BPF map (unprivileged_bpf_disabled blocks map // creation under `cargo test`). Production cost is one relaxed // increment under `#[cfg(test)]` only. #[cfg(test)] DNAT_DELETE_ATTEMPTS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed); unsafe { libbpf_sys::bpf_map_delete_elem(fd, dk.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>()); } ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:427` invokes that deletion for every forward SNAT close delta: ```rust // #2979: delete the dynamic reverse-NAT dnat_table entry this // SNAT'd session published at install. Keyed on the SAME forward // key + nat decision used by publish_dnat_table_entry (the Close // delta carries the forward key — it is gated on !is_reverse at // construction in session/expire.rs and session/mod.rs). A // non-SNAT session is a no-op (no rewrite_src -> no key). Only the // forward key publishes a dnat_table entry, so it is NOT repeated // for the reverse key below. super::checksum::delete_dnat_table_entry(dnat_fds, &delta.key, delta.decision.nat); ``` `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:831` is the live consumer: when no exact session marker exists for an embedded/reply packet, native-GRE steering depends only on presence of this DNAT key: ```rust // as the port key, so native GRE must use the same field here or the first // reply falls through to the kernel path. let dnat_port = if protocol == PROTO_ICMP { key.src_port } else { key.dst_port }; if dnat_lookup_v4(protocol, dst_v4, dnat_port).is_some() { return USERSPACE_SESSION_ACTION_REDIRECT; ```
Trace: 1. Two interface-SNAT sessions use the same protocol, egress address, and preserved source port but different remote endpoints. Both are legal: the full reverse session index can distinguish the remote endpoint, while interface mode has no port allocator reservation. 2. Each install publishes the same `dnat_table` key with `BPF_ANY`; because the XDP consumer tests only `.is_some()`, the single value acts as a shared steering marker. 3. Either session closes or expires. Its forward Close delta reaches `delete_dnat_table_entry`, which deletes the one map element without checking for another live holder. 4. The sibling session remains live. Ordinary exact replies can still hit `USERSPACE_SESSIONS`, but an inbound native-GRE embedded ICMP error has no exact session of its own and relies on `dnat_lookup_v4`/`dnat_lookup_v6` to enter userspace. 5. The lookup now misses, the packet falls away from the userspace embedded-ICMP reverse-NAT path, and PMTUD/traceroute feedback for the surviving flow is lost. The IPv6 helper has the same key lifetime defect.
Refutation attempt: I checked both source-NAT collision controls and the live classifier. Pool address-only reservations reject duplicate full reverse identities, but explicitly allow a different remote endpoint while the BPF key omits that endpoint; interface SNAT does not reserve a translated port at all. I also checked whether exact session steering makes the marker redundant: it covers normal replies, not the embedded ICMP packet described by the live `userspace-xdp` comments and lookup. Finally, I excluded the retired eBPF dataplane; this finding survives because the Rust userspace-XDP program reads the map in the live native-GRE path.
HPC/invariant check: The unsafe map syscall buffers have the correct fixed size and the native/network byte order matches the reader. The broken invariant is lifetime ownership: `one map key exists iff at least one live session needs steering`, while the code implements last-writer/first-closer semantics. No packet-path allocation is introduced by the bug; repair must avoid adding a contended RMW to every packet. Session install/close is the appropriate control point.
Why it matters: A short-lived flow can remove steering needed by an unrelated live flow. On native GRE, loss of ICMP Too-Big/Packet-Too-Big feedback creates a PMTUD blackhole and large TCP transfers can stall; traceroute and other embedded-ICMP diagnostics also fail. This is live userspace behavior, not retired eBPF residue.
Fix direction: Give the steering key explicit multi-holder ownership. The coordinator already serializes session deltas, so maintain a per-key holder count (including HA-imported sessions), publish on `0 -> 1`, and delete only on `1 -> 0`; reconcile counts on loss-of-sync. Alternatively change the map schema/lookup to include enough remote identity to make keys unique, but that must still support embedded ICMP parsing. Add v4/v6 regressions with two same-port interface/address-only SNAT flows to different remotes: closing either one must leave the marker until the last holder closes. Also protect static-DNAT keys from dynamic ownership transitions.
Labels: `nat`, `userspace-xdp`, `native-gre`, `pmtud`, `lifetime`, `vsrx-parity`
Dedup note: The refreshed 721-row index and issue history were searched by `dnat_v4_key_bytes`, `delete_dnat_table_entry`, reverse-NAT, SNAT close, shared key, PMTUD, and consequence. Closed #2979 found the opposite leak (no deletion) and added this unconditional delete; it did not model multiple live holders. Closed #4393 concerns missing HA publication. Closed #4399/#4438 concern 1:N Rust session indexes, not the userspace-XDP steering map. Open #6522 is a separate SNAT allocator holder-lifetime bug whose consequence is pool-port reuse. This has a different resource, call path, and production failure.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:198`. Independently retained in verify-R01-R12.md at the final target SHA.

#### R02: A zero-RG to first-RG clustered apply can expose LocalDelivery before HA inventory publication

Title: A zero-RG to first-RG clustered apply can expose LocalDelivery before HA inventory publication
Severity: Medium
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ha.rs:72-81` explicitly exempts LocalDelivery while the HA map is empty:

```rust
if !matches!(
    resolution.disposition,
    ForwardingDisposition::ForwardCandidate
        | ForwardingDisposition::MissingNeighbor
        | ForwardingDisposition::LocalDelivery
) {
    return resolution;
}
if resolution.disposition == ForwardingDisposition::LocalDelivery && ha_state.is_empty() {
    return resolution;
}
```

`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:365-369,383-388` applies helper status before refreshing and publishing HA state. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:26-37,277` sends no HA state when the current RG inventory is empty. `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:137` applies the forwarding snapshot before `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:221` updates cluster state. The topology preflight rejects standalone/cluster mode flips but not a zero-RG to first-RG edit within cluster mode.
Trace: 1. A valid chassis-cluster deployment starts with no redundancy-group stanza; the helper is already armed and its HA map remains empty because `syncHAStateLocked` sends nothing for an empty inventory. 2. An accepted day-2 commit adds the first RG and an RG-owned interface-NAT local address. 3. The daemon applies the forwarding snapshot and helper status before publishing the new HA inventory. 4. During that interval, an RG-owned interface-NAT packet resolves as `LocalDelivery`; the Rust empty-map shortcut treats it as standalone and skips owner-RG enforcement. 5. A permitted one-shot UDP/control packet can reach the inactive node before the later HA publication closes the window.
Refutation attempt: The original source report's literal cold-helper-start trace was refuted: Rust starts disarmed, startup applies HA before arming, and cross-mode topology changes require restart. Independent verification then tested the topology guard and zero-RG validity and found the narrower same-mode transition remains reachable. The explicit RG-transition fence covers activation callbacks, not this accepted config-apply ordering, and host-inbound policy is orthogonal to ownership.
HPC/invariant check: ArcSwap publication is coherent and memory-safe. The semantic defect is the collapse of `standalone` and `clustered but HA inventory currently empty`; a tri-state readiness bit closes it without adding a packet-path lock.
Why it matters: A valid day-2 HA configuration change can briefly admit an RG-owned local packet on the inactive node. For IKE, management, or other permitted datagram services, one accepted packet can create split-brain behavior even though the system otherwise promises fail-closed ownership enforcement.
Fix direction: Represent HA as `Standalone | ClusterUninitialized | Ready(map)` and fail closed in the middle state. Fence userspace control whenever an accepted snapshot changes HA ownership inventory, publish and acknowledge matching HA state before re-enable, and add a zero-RG to first-RG live-apply regression.
Labels: `ha`, `day-2-apply`, `local-delivery`, `startup-order`, `fail-closed`, `vsrx-parity`
Dedup note: Independent body-level comparison found no open issue owning the intra-cluster zero-RG to first-RG ordering. #6187 concerns standalone/cluster supervisor boundaries; #6707 concerns rejected policy snapshots.
Verified against origin/master: Still present at origin/master `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea` at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:369`. Independently retained in verify-R01-R12.md at the final target SHA.

#### R03: Full IKE exchange table serializes admitted initiations through an O(4096) eviction scan

Title: Full IKE exchange table serializes admitted initiations through an O(4096) eviction scan
Severity: Medium
Confidence: High
Gate verdict: MATERIAL
Evidence: `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ipsec.rs:201` establishes an attacker-fillable cap of 4,096 entries and oldest eviction: ```rust /// #6471: hard cap on tracked live IKE exchanges per node. Far above any /// legitimate site-to-site count on this class of box (hundreds); the bound /// keeps a forged-initiation flood on an IKE-permitting zone from growing /// the table without limit. On full, the OLDEST entry is evicted (see /// [`IkeExchangeTable::seed`]). pub(in crate::afxdp) const IKE_EXCHANGE_TABLE_CAP: usize = 4096; ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ipsec.rs:232` includes attacker-controlled initiator SPI in the key, so one peer/local pair can create arbitrary distinct entries: ```rust #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] pub(in crate::afxdp) struct IkeExchangeKey { pub(in crate::afxdp) initiator_spi: u64, pub(in crate::afxdp) peer_ip: IpAddr, pub(in crate::afxdp) local_ip: IpAddr, } ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ipsec.rs:292` places every worker behind one mutex: ```rust pub(in crate::afxdp) struct IkeExchangeTable { entries: Mutex<FastMap<IkeExchangeKey, u64>>, // key -> last-seen monotonic ns } impl IkeExchangeTable { pub(in crate::afxdp) fn new() -> Self { Self { entries: Mutex::new(FastMap::default()), } ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ipsec.rs:319` scans every entry to find the oldest while holding that mutex for each new key once full: ```rust pub(in crate::afxdp) fn seed(&self, key: IkeExchangeKey, now_ns: u64) { let mut entries = self.lock_entries(); if let Some(seen) = entries.get_mut(&key) { *seen = now_ns; return; } if entries.len() >= IKE_EXCHANGE_TABLE_CAP && let Some(oldest) = entries .iter() .min_by_key(|(_, seen)| seen) ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:1132` admits initiations according to host-inbound configuration and then seeds them: ```rust // #4323 Option B: gate a NEW inbound IKE initiation on host-inbound. crate::afxdp::forwarding::IpsecAdmissionClass::NewInboundIke => { if let Some(from_zone_id) = ike_host_inbound_deny_zone(flow, meta, dst_port, ingress_zone_override, now_secs, worker_ctx) { return IpsecPassthroughOutcome::Denied { from_zone_id }; } // #6471: the initiation was ADMITTED — seed the exchange so its // established follow-ups (Responder SPI set) are recognized. A ``` `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:1148` performs the global-table call directly in the packet stage: ```rust ) { worker_ctx.ike_exchanges.seed( crate::afxdp::forwarding::IkeExchangeKey::new( initiator_spi, flow.src_ip, flow.dst_ip, ), now_ns, ); ``` The stated upstream rate bound is optional. `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_stages.rs:488` passes immediately when no screen profile exists: ```rust now_secs: u64, screen: &mut ScreenState, counters: &mut BatchCounters, worker_ctx: &WorkerContext, ) -> StageOutcome<ScreenCheckOutcome> { if !screen.has_profiles() { return StageOutcome::Continue(ScreenCheckOutcome::Pass); } ``` `userspace-dp/src/screen/packet.rs:86` also defines a configured zero UDP threshold as disabled: ```rust pub syn_frag: bool, pub source_route: bool, pub icmp_flood_threshold: u32, // packets per second, 0 = disabled pub udp_flood_threshold: u32,  // packets per second, 0 = disabled pub syn_flood_threshold: u32,  // SYN packets per second per zone, 0 = disabled ```
Trace: 1. A DNAT/static-NAT-to-self or native-GRE-inner IKE endpoint is permitted by the ingress zone's host-inbound IKE service. This is the documented AF_XDP secondary path. 2. An attacker sends syntactically valid zero-responder-SPI initiations and varies the 64-bit initiator SPI. Stage 11 admits and seeds each unique key. 3. After 4,096 keys, every additional initiation acquires the node-global mutex and iterates the entire `FastMap` to compute the minimum timestamp, then removes and inserts. 4. Concurrent packet workers targeting any secondary-path IKE exchange block on the same cache line/mutex. The attack therefore converts line-rate admitted UDP into serialized O(4,096) work before reinjection to the kernel IKE daemon. 5. With no screen profile, or `udp_flood_threshold=0`, stage 10 imposes no rate bound. Host-inbound IKE permission is an access policy, not a flood limiter.
Refutation attempt: I checked whether the cap, lazy expiry, screen stage, primary-path nftables, or strongSwan cost bounded the Rust work. The cap bounds memory but is exactly what activates the repeated full scan. Lazy expiry occurs on lookup and does not make full-table seed eviction O(1). Screen profiles are optional and zero disables UDP flood control. Direct interface-IP IKE uses the primary path, but the documented DNAT/static-NAT/native-GRE secondary path is live. Kernel IKE processing may itself be expensive, but this scan happens first and adds a global cross-worker serialization point.
HPC/invariant check: There is no memory-unsafety or integer overflow. The violated performance invariant is `bounded control table must have bounded per-packet maintenance independent of occupancy`. A `FastMap` iteration touches thousands of noncontiguous cache lines under a single mutex; every worker then contends on that mutex's cache line. The key clone is allocation-free, but lock hold time and cache misses are attacker-amplified.
Why it matters: An operator must be able to permit IKE without making the userspace packet workers vulnerable to deterministic global lock contention. Saturating this secondary-path table can consume packet cores and delay unrelated IKE/control processing, causing tunnel setup/rekey/DPD failures and broader packet-loop latency on affected workers.
Fix direction: Replace the full scan with bounded eviction metadata: an indexed min-heap (`O(log n)`), timing wheel, or generation-tagged FIFO/LRU queue with stale-node validation and a strict bounded-node budget. Sharding by local endpoint can reduce mutex contention, but each shard still needs bounded eviction. Add a full-cap benchmark/test that asserts one new seed does not visit all entries and a multi-thread contention benchmark independent of optional screen configuration.
Labels: `ipsec`, `ike`, `dos`, `performance`, `lock-contention`, `packet-latency`, `vsrx-parity`

Open #6700 concerns xfrmi/plaintext interface modeling, #6542 strongSwan teardown debt, and #5619 XFRM plaintext policy. The historical O(4096) item concerns a rejected V_min bucket scan, a different subsystem and call path. No issue covers the global IKE exchange eviction scan.
