## R61

**Title:** Managed service file convergence suppresses retries after runtime reload failure

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:480-505` declares convergence solely from file bytes/removal, and chrony consumes that edge at `:508-576` while swallowing command failures:

```go
if err == nil && string(current) == content {
    return false, nil
}
...
if out, err := chronyCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
    slog.Warn("failed to reload chrony sources", "err", err, "output", string(out))
}
...
if !sourcesChanged && !thresholdChanged {
    return
}
```

Rsyslog follows the same edge at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:993-1004`: `changed := reconcileSyslogDropins(...)`; restart failure is logged, and a later identical apply sees `changed == false`. The SSH removal path at `:1582-1600` removes the drop-in, returns a reload error, then a later apply takes `if !hadDropIn { return nil }`. The SSH update path restores readable prior bytes after a failed reload, so the durable lost-retry example there is specifically removal; chrony and rsyslog retain the newly converged files.

**Trace:** Active config reaches `applySystemNTP`, syslog rendering, or `applySSHConfig`; the managed file is atomically written/removed; runtime reload/restart fails; only a log/error is produced and no runtime-acknowledged generation or retry debt is retained; the next full apply compares against already-converged disk state and skips the runtime action. Runtime may therefore remain on the previous service configuration until an unrelated file change or process restart.

**Refutation attempt:** I traced every caller and looked for a timer, degraded retry owner, service-generation marker, or unconditional reload. None exists for these paths. Re-running the whole daemon apply is insufficient because the file comparator suppresses the action. SSH write/update rollback narrows that subcase but does not protect removal; chrony and rsyslog do not roll back file content. Existing tests assert rendering/file idempotence and command invocation on a change, not failure followed by an identical apply.

**HPC/invariant check:** Keep file reconciliation idempotent and bounded, but track runtime convergence separately from disk convergence. Retry only the failed service/generation with bounded backoff; do not restart all services on every apply.

**Why it matters:** A committed NTP, audit-log, or SSH service change can be durably represented on disk while the live daemon continues enforcing the old state with no automatic repair.

**Fix direction:** Make reload/restart return an error and retain per-service retry debt keyed by desired file digest. For SSH removal, either restore the removed file on reload failure or retain explicit removal-reload debt. Clear debt only after runtime acknowledgement.

**Labels:** `daemon`, `managed-files`, `chrony`, `rsyslog`, `sshd`, `retry-debt`, `runtime-convergence`

**Dedup note:** Complete open-body and dedup-index searches found adjacent prior items about unvalidated service renderer strings and IPsec/FRR reload convergence, but no issue owns this shared managed-file-before-runtime-ack root.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. Review HEAD and `origin/master` both equal `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R62

**Title:** Shrinking the userspace interface allowlist leaves RSS and adaptive coalescence changes on released NICs

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:292-314` derives only the new allowlist and passes it to both reconcilers:

```go
rssAllowed = dpuserspace.UserspaceBoundLinuxInterfaces(cfg)
...
reapplyRSSIndirection(rssEnabled, workers, rssAllowed)
d.applyStep0Tunables(..., rssAllowed)
```

`pkg/daemon/rss_indirection.go:149-207` restores or applies only names in `allowed`; `len(allowed) == 0` is an immediate no-op. `pkg/daemon/host_tunables_daemon.go:117-123` likewise invokes coalescence only for current names. Prior adaptive state is retained in `prior.mlx5Adaptive`, but `:145-148` deliberately leaves those captures in place during runtime transitions and `:245-278` restores them only at daemon shutdown.

**Trace:** Config A gives userspace ownership of NICs A and B, so RSS and/or coalescence are changed on both and coalescence originals are captured. Config B removes B from the userspace-bound set. Both reconcilers iterate only A; no `previous - current` pass restores B. B is released to another owner with xpfd's RSS table/coalescence settings still live until shutdown.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked worker-count reductions, RSS disable, userspace disable, host-tunable opt-out, capture maps, shutdown restore, and tests. Worker-to-one and explicit RSS-disable restore only the current allowlist. Userspace disable restores neighbor and host-scope state but has no current-vs-prior coalescence release pass. RSS stores no prior owned-interface set at all. Tests do not exercise `{A,B} -> {A}`.

**HPC/invariant check:** Preserve O(number of touched NICs) behavior. Maintain an explicit prior-owned set and reconcile `released = prior - current`; only restore values xpfd captured or an RSS default it installed. A retry debt entry is needed when release restoration fails.

**Why it matters:** A NIC returned to kernel or another service can retain concentrated RSS and latency-oriented coalescence settings, causing persistent throughput/latency behavior outside xpfd's current ownership.

**Fix direction:** Record successfully touched RSS interfaces and use the existing coalescence capture keys as ownership. Restore released names before dropping ownership, retaining failed names as retry debt; add `{A,B}->{A}` and disable-transition tests.

**Labels:** `daemon`, `userspace-dp`, `rss`, `coalescence`, `interface-ownership`, `runtime-reconcile`

**Dedup note:** GH#5328's RSS survivor is `indirectionTableMatches` accepting a subset of active queues on a currently managed NIC. It does not cover allowlist withdrawal or coalescence restoration. GH#5250's scanner/coalescence item is parser churn, also distinct.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R63

**Title:** Failed host-inbound conntrack revocation loses retry debt

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** The security dependency is stated and implemented at `pkg/daemon/host_inbound_conntrack_flush.go:14-39`. The only live caller is after successful nft host-inbound install at `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:548-558`. The failure loop at `host_inbound_conntrack_flush.go:277-295` is:

```go
for _, family := range []netlink.InetFamily{unix.AF_INET, unix.AF_INET6} {
    n, err := conntrackDeleteFilters(family, filter)
    if err != nil {
        slog.Warn("host-inbound conntrack reconcile failed ...", "family", family, "err", err)
        continue
    }
    flushed += n
}
```

There is no retained family/filter debt or timer. The installed chain leads with `ct state established,related accept`, and table replacement does not revoke those old conntrack entries (`:16-35`).

**Trace:** A service is removed from the current host-inbound set; nft rules install successfully; the post-install conntrack sweep builds the current deny filter; deletion for one or both families fails transiently; the error is logged and the function returns. Existing direct-kernel sessions continue hitting established/related accept. No future work is scheduled; only another config apply happens to call the sweep again.

**Refutation attempt:** I searched all callers, periodic reconciliation, conntrack GC ownership, apply failure propagation, and tests. The function is invoked once from the nft apply tail. A later operator apply would retry by reconstruction, but there is no guaranteed later apply and no debt consumer. Tests cover filter matching and successful deletion, not a failed deletion followed by autonomous retry. Userspace session per-hit reevaluation protects a different dataplane path and does not revoke Linux conntrack.

**HPC/invariant check:** Retry work must remain bounded to the current host-inbound filter and two address families. Recompute the filter from current config before each retry so stale debt cannot delete newly permitted flows; serialize with nft apply or bind debt to the installed generation.

**Why it matters:** A credentialed or otherwise established direct-kernel management/session flow can retain authorization after the operator removes the corresponding host-inbound service.

**Fix direction:** Have per-family deletion return status, retain failed-family generation debt, and consume it on bounded backoff/status reconcile. Clear debt on success or when a newer host-inbound generation supersedes it.

**Labels:** `daemon`, `nftables`, `conntrack`, `host-inbound`, `authorization-revocation`, `retry-debt`

**Dedup note:** GH#5858 concerns established userspace transit sessions after an interface input-filter change. No supplied open issue or dedup row owns failed Linux host-inbound conntrack revocation retry.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R64

**Title:** A dead same-endpoint management listener is observed but never reconciled

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/api/listener.go:68-86` marks an unexpected Serve exit:

```go
case err := <-serveErr:
    ...
    leg.dead.Store(true)
    return
```

`EffectiveHTTPAddr` reports it dead at `:158-167`, but same-address HTTP and HTTPS calls return before testing `dead` at `:175-192` and `:204-229`:

```go
if s.httpLeg != nil && s.httpLeg.srv.Addr == addr {
    return nil
}
...
case s.httpsLeg != nil && s.httpsLeg.srv.Addr == addr:
    return nil
```

The daemon observes failed status at `pkg/daemon/management.go:160-180`, while reconcile invokes listener methods only when endpoint fingerprints change at `:208-229`.

**Trace:** A previously healthy HTTP/HTTPS leg exits unexpectedly. Its `dead` flag becomes true and status changes to Failed. Desired endpoint and management `m.cur` fingerprint remain unchanged. A later config reconcile skips the daemon's address-change branch; even a direct same-address server reconcile no-ops on `srv.Addr`. The dead leg is never recreated until an endpoint change or process restart.

**Refutation attempt:** I merged the A7 and A8 reports into this one root and traced both layers. Status visibility is not repair. Bind-failure debt applies to replacement attempts, not unexpected post-convergence exits. `TestServeExitDoesNotDeadlockConcurrentWait` covers dead-state publication and shutdown joining, not same-address recreation. GH#6721 starts with boot bind failure and `m.srv == nil`; this root starts after successful service with a non-nil dead leg.

**HPC/invariant check:** Listener convergence must be `(desired endpoint, live serving state)`. Recreate under `lifeMu` with make-before-break where possible; the already-dead socket needs no drain. Preserve auth-slot ownership and avoid holding daemon `m.mu` across an unbounded operation.

**Why it matters:** Management status correctly reports failure, but the service can remain unavailable forever despite repeated identical reconciles.

**Fix direction:** Include `dead.Load()` in the same-address no-op conditions and have management reconciliation call the leg reconciler when effective status is dead. Add HTTP and HTTPS unexpected-exit/same-address recovery tests.

**Labels:** `api`, `daemon`, `management`, `listener`, `liveness`, `reconcile`

**Dedup note:** GH#6721 is initial boot bind failure; GH#6717 is async retiring-listener auth loosening. Neither owns post-convergence unexpected exit plus same-endpoint no-op. A7/A8 source traces are merged here exactly once.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R65

**Title:** Kernel lo0 mirror omits valid flexible-match and widens terms

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** A compiled term owns `FlexMatch *FlexMatchConfig` at `pkg/config/types_system.go:1392-1417`. Userspace snapshot lowering explicitly emits it at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:310-381`. In contrast, `pkg/nftables/netlink_spec.go:71-106` defines `Lo0FilterTerm` without any FlexMatch field, and `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:194-222` copies every listed match dimension but no `term.FlexMatch`. `pkg/nftables/netlink_lo0.go:93-135` therefore has no flexible-byte predicate in `applyMatches`.

```go
type Lo0FilterTerm struct {
    ...
    Protocols []string
    SourcePorts []string
    DestinationPorts []string
    ...
    IsFragment bool
}
```

The strict validator at `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:918-969` rejects malformed/multiple flex forms, not a valid single representable one.

**Trace:** A valid lo0 firewall term compiles with a flexible byte-offset match. The userspace snapshot carries and Rust enforces it. The kernel mirror converter has no representation for it, so the generated nft rule includes the term's remaining predicates/action without the flex condition. Kernel-delivered host traffic can match a broader set than configured.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked strict validation, the text nft oracle, netlink DTO, converter, builder, Rust matcher, and tests. The validator does not ban FlexMatch on lo0. Neither kernel renderer adds it later. Existing lo0 parity tests cover addresses, ports, DSCP, ICMP, TCP flags, fragments, actions, and malformed-address fail-closed behavior, but not a valid flexible match.

**HPC/invariant check:** Kernel/user filter lowering must preserve every accepted match dimension or reject the term before either dataplane publishes. A fixed-width flex match is constant work per packet and does not alter table cardinality.

**Why it matters:** Depending on term action and order, host control-plane traffic outside the configured byte pattern can be accepted or denied. For an accept term followed by deny, omission is a direct policy widening.

**Fix direction:** Add a typed flex-match field to `Lo0FilterTerm`, copy it in `toNftLo0Term`, lower layer-3/layer-4 offset/length/value/mask in both netlink and text paths, and add parity/wire tests. If nft cannot represent a valid form, fail the lo0 plan closed.

**Labels:** `daemon`, `nftables`, `lo0`, `firewall-filter`, `flexible-match`, `policy-parity`, `fail-open`

**Dedup note:** GH#6512 owns partially malformed lo0 address lists. No open body or dedup row owns omission of valid FlexMatch from the kernel mirror.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R66

**Title:** First apply leaves a list-only tunnel outside its routing-instance VRF

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** Step 0a runs before tunnel creation and explicitly treats not-found as warning-only at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:208-238`:

```go
// BEFORE applyInterfaceReconcile creates tunnel/xfrmi devices
if err := d.routing.BindInterfaceToVRF(linuxName, ri.Name); err != nil {
    slog.Warn("failed to bind interface to VRF", ...)
}
```

`collectAppliedTunnels` carries list intent in `RIListMember` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run_routehelpers.go:59-114`). The creation tail calls `reconcileVRFClaimLocked` at `pkg/routing/tunnel.go:887-913`, but list-only intent takes the observation-only branch at `:1104-1123`; if the new link has no master, `observeListClaimLocked` returns at `:1193-1207`:

```go
if tc.RIListMember != "" {
    t.observeListClaimLocked(tc, link)
    return
}
...
if master == 0 { return }
```

**Trace:** On the first apply, a routing-instance lists a tunnel not yet present. Step 0a bind fails ENODEV and is intentionally ignored. Interface reconciliation then creates the tunnel and supplies `RIListMember`. The tunnel manager assumes step 0a owns list binds and only observes a master; the just-created link has none, so no bind occurs. A second full apply can bind it, but no first-apply repair is guaranteed.

**Refutation attempt:** I traced interface ordering, tunnel collection, direct-stanza precedence, claim bookkeeping, link events, and tests. Direct `tunnel routing-instance` takes the active bind branch and is not affected. `TestTunnelVRFListVetoWithFailedBindNoClaim` at `pkg/routing/tunnel_reconcile_test.go:1243-1258` explicitly expects no claim after the failed pre-bind shape; it protects unbind ownership but also confirms no creation-tail repair. I found no periodic full step-0a retry.

**HPC/invariant check:** Preserve stanza-over-list precedence and the identity-gated unbind invariant. The creation tail can perform one bounded bind only when `RoutingInstance == ""`, `RIListMember != ""`, and observed master is zero; record a claim only after bind success.

**Why it matters:** The tunnel can route in the default namespace instead of its configured VRF on initial activation, violating isolation/routing intent until another apply happens.

**Fix direction:** After tunnel creation, actively bind list-only members when step 0a could not have succeeded, or reorder tunnel creation before list binding. Add a one-apply integration test asserting the kernel master is `vrf-<RI>`.

**Labels:** `daemon`, `routing`, `tunnel`, `vrf`, `routing-instance`, `first-apply`, `isolation`

**Dedup note:** Supplied tunnel/xfrmi issues concern zone adjudication, neighbor resolution, naming, or feature support. None owns the pre-create list bind plus observation-only creation tail.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R67

**Title:** Kernel lo0 mirror drops tolerant unknown protocol and ICMP fail-closed markers

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** Unknown protocols and symbolic ICMP values are strict errors but tolerated warnings on Load/SyncApply at `pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_filter.go:12-37` and `:83-102`. The compiled term retains raw protocols and unknown markers (`pkg/config/types_system.go:1304-1332`). The userspace builder emits protocols and ICMP unrepresentable flags at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:130-137` and `:294-308`; Rust rejects the whole candidate at `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs:545-559`, `:609-623`, and `:809-835`.

The kernel DTO has only `Protocols`, resolved `ICMPTypes`, and resolved `ICMPCodes` (`pkg/nftables/netlink_spec.go:89-98`). Its builder applies protocol only when `lo0Protocols` returns a nonempty set and applies only resolved ICMP bytes (`pkg/nftables/netlink_lo0.go:100-123`):

```go
if protos := lo0Protocols(t.Protocols); len(protos) > 0 {
    a.l4protoSet(protos)
}
...
if len(t.ICMPTypes) > 0 { a.icmpType(...) }
```

**Trace:** A legacy/persisted/peer config contains a nonempty unknown protocol or unknown ICMP type/code. Lenient compile warns and retains enough state for userspace fail-closed rejection. The lo0 converter omits the marker; unknown protocol resolution yields no kernel predicate, while unknown-only ICMP yields empty resolved bytes. The kernel term is installed with that dimension unconstrained even though Rust keeps its previous good snapshot.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked strict and lenient paths, compiled fields, Go snapshot markers, Rust preflight/last-good behavior, netlink/text lo0 renderers, and downstream error propagation. Strict operator commits are protected; the live ingress is Load/SyncApply/rollback compatibility. No later lo0 gate sees `UnknownICMP*`, and raw unknown protocol is logged/dropped rather than poisoning the term or plan. GH#6512's address marker path demonstrates a separate marker was added; it does not cover protocol/ICMP.

**HPC/invariant check:** Every tolerant unrepresentable marker accepted by config must have identical fail-closed semantics on all active dataplane mirrors. Rejecting one lo0 plan at build time is bounded and preferable to silently omitting a predicate.

**Why it matters:** The kernel host-input path can enforce a widened term while the userspace path retains old policy, producing both policy bypass risk and mode-dependent behavior.

**Fix direction:** Carry protocol/ICMP unrepresentable markers into `Lo0FilterTerm` and fail the nft plan closed, or poison only the affected term to never match under a documented invariant. Add lenient lo0 parity tests for unknown-only and mixed known/unknown lists.

**Labels:** `config`, `daemon`, `nftables`, `lo0`, `firewall-filter`, `lenient-load`, `snapshot-integrity`

**Dedup note:** GH#6512 is the malformed-address sibling. No exact unknown-protocol/unknown-ICMP kernel-marker omission appears in the complete open bodies or dedup index.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R68

**Title:** Oversized FRR policy omission leaves a dangling BGP route-map attachment that denies all affected routes

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL, with the source reports' permit-all consequence corrected to implicit deny

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/frr/policy_render.go:263-286` skips a policy definition when expansion exceeds `MaxRouteMapSequences`:

```go
if n := config.RouteMapSequenceCount(ps); n > config.MaxRouteMapSequences {
    slog.Warn("skipping oversized route-map policy ...")
    continue
}
```

The composed-chain sibling returns an empty definition at `:831-849`. Yet protocol rendering still sees the config policy as defined and emits `neighbor ... route-map ... in/out` at `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:496-527`. The repository comments/tests claim an undefined map permits all, but that claim is false for the target FRR line. The repository records FRR 10.6 deployment in `_Log.md:36186`; official FRR stable/10.6 `bgpd/bgp_route.c:2092-2097` and `:2152-2157` return `RMAP_DENY` when `route_map_lookup_by_name` is null:

```c
if (rmap_name) {
    rmap = route_map_lookup_by_name(rmap_name);
    if (!rmap)
        return RMAP_DENY;
}
```

Primary source: https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/blob/stable/10.6/bgpd/bgp_route.c#L2092-L2097 . The same behavior was mechanically checked in official stable/8.4, 9.1, 10.0, 10.4, 10.6, and master source.

**Trace:** A persisted, peer-synced, or rollback config exceeds the route-map sequence cap. The lenient gate warns. FRR policy rendering omits the standalone or composed definition to avoid poisoning the batched reload. BGP rendering independently emits an attachment because the policy exists in `PolicyStatements`. FRR stores/uses the named attachment but cannot resolve the map, and inbound/outbound modifier code returns deny. All affected routes are filtered until the policy is reduced or detached.

**Refutation attempt:** I tested the central fail-open claim against repository tests, installed tooling, official docs, and official FRR source. `vtysh` is unavailable in this worktree, so no live FRR reproduction was possible. FRR's documented default deny for an existing route-map with no match did not by itself settle undefined-map behavior; official bgpd source did. It explicitly denies missing maps. Thus the confidentiality/policy-widening claim is refuted, but the reachable omission/attachment mechanism remains a meaningful availability/routing-correctness defect. The repository's `TestGenerateProtocols_BGPImportUndefinedNoDangling` and related comments assert permit-all without executing FRR and should be corrected.

**HPC/invariant check:** A referenced policy definition and its attachment must be emitted atomically. The bounded sequence cap is valid; fallback should not exceed it or poison the reload. A small explicit fail-closed map can preserve denial deterministically, but operators also need apply failure/health rather than silent accepted outage.

**Why it matters:** A compatible legacy/HA config can cleanly reload the rest of FRR while withdrawing all inbound or outbound routes on attached neighbors, potentially causing a routing outage. This is not the reported route leak.

**Fix direction:** Filter BGP references through a rendered-policy set, or emit a bounded explicit deny route-map under the referenced name and surface degraded apply state. Prefer rejecting/quarantining the peer/rollback snapshot before FRR if compatibility policy allows. Correct stale permit-all comments/tests and add an FRR integration assertion for undefined maps.

**Labels:** `frr`, `bgp`, `route-map`, `lenient-load`, `availability`, `render-dependency`, `documentation-correction`

**Dedup note:** No supplied open issue or dedup row owns oversized-policy omission plus surviving BGP attachment. Existing undefined-reference guards concern genuinely absent config policies and do not catch a configured policy omitted later by the sequence belt.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, repository mechanism at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`; FRR consequence independently checked against official stable/10.6 source.

## R69

**Title:** REST commit holder check and callback turnover can substitute another candidate

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/api/config.go:223-266` obtains a session, checks holder, then invokes an unscoped callback:

```go
if err := s.store.EnsureConfigHolder(sessionID); err != nil { ... }
...
compiled, err := s.commitFn(r.Context(), "")
```

`EnsureConfigHolder` holds `Store.mu` only for the check (`pkg/configstore/store_lock.go:63-73`). The REST callback at `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_servers.go:82-85` carries only context/comment. It can wait for `applySem` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_commit.go:146-175`), then `commitWithGenBinding` snapshots whichever candidate is current at `:98-126`. `CommitWithDescriptionGen` checks only candidate generation (`pkg/configstore/store_commit.go:122-129`), not session holder. Session A can exit and discard its candidate at `pkg/configstore/store_lock.go:229-245`; B can enter and create a new candidate at `:138-174`.

**Trace:** A owns the REST config lock and calls commit. `EnsureConfigHolder(A)` succeeds. Before the callback acquires `applySem`, A exits/disconnect cleanup or lease turnover releases its lock; B enters and edits candidate B. A's callback later acquires `applySem`, compiles candidate B with its current generation, and commits it. Generation binding prevents an edit between compile and promote, but it does not bind the transaction to A or A's candidate epoch.

**Refutation attempt:** I traced normal commit, commit-confirmed, pending-confirm shortcut, apply serialization, candidate generations, lock leases, exit, and re-entry. The pending-confirm/clean-candidate shortcut calls `ConfirmCommitAs(sessionID)` and rechecks identity, so that narrow path is protected. Normal callbacks lose session identity. `applySem` serializes promoters but does not cover REST holder check, configure exit, or editing. Candidate generation detects mutation after snapshot, not candidate ownership substitution before snapshot.

**HPC/invariant check:** Holder identity and candidate generation must be validated in the same store critical section as promotion, while hardware preflight may remain outside the lock. Bind an opaque `(sessionID, candidateEpoch, generation)` token and reject turnover; do not hold `Store.mu` across apply.

**Why it matters:** One REST caller can unintentionally commit and apply another operator's staged candidate, violating configuration authorization and audit attribution.

**Fix direction:** Thread `sessionID` through REST commit callbacks and add session-aware generation-bound store methods that verify current effective holder plus epoch immediately before promotion. Add a deterministic A-check/B-turnover/A-callback test.

**Labels:** `api`, `rest`, `configstore`, `commit`, `authorization`, `toctou`, `candidate-generation`

**Dedup note:** GH#5962 concerns RG0 authority changing around a different commit preflight. No open issue owns config-holder turnover between REST check and unscoped callback.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R70

**Title:** Slow BGP API reader can pin a handler and vtysh child indefinitely

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/api/routing.go:147-241` streams routes synchronously. Every 1024 records its callback runs:

```go
if ferr := bw.Flush(); ferr != nil { return ferr }
if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok { f.Flush() }
```

The final flush is also unchecked for duration. `pkg/api/server.go:363-376` deliberately leaves `WriteTimeout` at zero; the claim that per-handler deadlines bound responses is not true for this endpoint. `pkg/frr/status_parse.go:397-445` synchronously scans vtysh stdout and invokes the callback before cancellation/reaping. `pkg/frr/vtysh.go:121-139` uses `exec.CommandContext(ctx, ...)`, but the request context has no deadline and remains live while a connected slow client stalls writes.

**Trace:** An authenticated client requests BGP routes and reads very slowly or stops reading without disconnecting. The response flush blocks once socket buffers fill. The callback cannot return; `StreamBGPRoutes` stops scanning stdout; vtysh blocks when its pipe fills. Cancellation and `finish()` are after the callback/scan exits, so handler goroutine, child, pipe, and connection remain pinned. The 100,000-route cap bounds bytes/CPU after progress, not elapsed time while blocked.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked HTTP server timeouts, request contexts, write errors, route cap, scanner limits, process cancellation, `WaitDelay`, auth, and concurrency controls. Disconnects and write errors cancel correctly, but a still-connected nonreader produces neither. `WaitDelay` matters only after context cancellation. SSE explains why global `WriteTimeout` is zero, but there is no BGP-local deadline or limiter. I found no BGP handler semaphore.

**HPC/invariant check:** Preserve bounded-memory streaming and do not impose a global timeout that breaks SSE. Add a BGP-specific elapsed-time/write-progress budget and a small concurrency limiter. Child cancellation must occur when either budget expires.

**Why it matters:** A small number of authenticated slow readers can accumulate long-lived vtysh children and handler/socket resources, degrading the management and routing control planes.

**Fix direction:** Wrap this route-stream request in a finite context, use response-controller write deadlines or a timeout-aware writer, and limit concurrent full-RIB streams. Ensure timeout cancellation closes/reaps vtysh.

**Labels:** `api`, `bgp`, `frr`, `vtysh`, `slow-reader`, `resource-exhaustion`, `timeout`

**Dedup note:** GH#6552 covers an unconditional gRPC journalctl fork and GH#6553 covers uncancelled NAT RPC walks. Neither owns REST BGP downstream backpressure pinning vtysh.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R71

**Title:** Event-engine edge latch advances before bounded queue admission

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/eventengine/engine.go:1119-1183` evaluates under `e.mu` and arms the latch before returning a trigger:

```go
if policyHasTriggerOn(pol) {
    rt.onLatched[ev.Name] = true
}
triggered = append(triggered, ...)
```

`HandleEvent` classifies and calls `enqueue` only afterward (`:548-574`). The bounded queue path at `:624-669` returns no admission result; when full of other policies it only increments/logs a drop. `withinMatches` at `:1357-1377` suppresses all later at/above-threshold events while `onLatched` remains true and clears it only after the window count drops below the threshold.

**Trace:** The action worker is delayed, and 64 distinct policy actions occupy the queue. A different edge-triggered policy crosses its threshold. Evaluation sets `onLatched=true`. Its valid action cannot be admitted because the queue is full of other policies, so it is dropped. Subsequent events keep the count at/above threshold and are suppressed as already fired. The remediation never ran and does not retry until the event level falls below threshold and crosses again.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked same-policy supersede, concurrent producer locking, cooldown, stale revision checks, action retry, worker shutdown, and edge tests. Supersede fixes duplicate occupancy but deliberately returns false for a full distinct-policy queue. Retry applies only to admitted actions. Existing edge tests prove one fire per sustained level; queue tests prove drops are bounded; none couples a queue-full drop to latch rollback. GH#5250's event item is a different latch keyed per event across multiple clauses.

**HPC/invariant check:** Keep evaluation windows and the 64-slot queue bounded. Latch transition must be committed only on successful admission, or rolled back under `e.mu` using the same policy semantic revision. Respect lock order (`e.mu` versus `enqueueMu`) to avoid deadlock.

**Why it matters:** A transient queue saturation can permanently consume a threshold crossing, silently skipping configured remediation for a sustained fault.

**Fix direction:** Make enqueue return an admission verdict and arm the edge only after admission, or attach a crossing token and clear the exact latch on rejection if policy/revision still matches. Add a 64-distinct-policy saturation test.

**Labels:** `eventengine`, `queue`, `edge-trigger`, `latch`, `backpressure`, `lost-action`

**Dedup note:** GH#5250/ps-review-042 owns shared per-event latch state across multiple `within` clauses. This root is admission ordering for one crossing and is not a duplicate.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R72

**Title:** Mixed-family flow-export instance cross-fans flows to wrong-family collectors

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** `pkg/flowexport/manager.go:181-239` walks inet and inet6 into one collector slice. `CollectorConfig` receives address/source/template but no family; only aggregate booleans survive:

```go
collectors = append(collectors, CollectorConfig{Address: addr, SourceAddress: srcAddr, Template: tmpl})
if fe.isV6 { servesInet6 = true } else { servesInet = true }
```

`groupCollectorsByTemplate` partitions only by template (`:352-379`). Every v9 group gets the same aggregate `ServesInet/ServesInet6` at `:445-457`; IPFIX repeats this at `:506-517`. The daemon gates the lead group once and exports to every group at `pkg/daemon/daemon_flowexport.go:524-543` and `:581-594`.

**Trace:** One supported sampling instance contains IPv4 collector A and IPv6 collector B. Collector family is discarded during flattening. With one template, A and B share one group; with distinct templates, every group still receives both aggregate family flags. An IPv4 session passes the instance-level lead gate and is sent by every group, including B; IPv6 likewise reaches A.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked strict validators, version partitioning, template grouping, sampling-counter sharing, daemon callback family gates, and tests. `pkg/config/sampling_instance_conflict_test.go:70-81` explicitly accepts one multi-family instance. Version binding prevents v9/IPFIX double-export but does not preserve address family. Closed #2462 fixed cross-instance flattening, not same-instance family routing. Existing template tests use one family or assert deterministic grouping, so they do not refute this shape.

**HPC/invariant check:** Keep a single sampling decision/counter per instance and deterministic build-time groups. Add family to the group key or a family mask per collector/group; do not add per-packet collector resolution.

**Why it matters:** Records are sent to collectors outside their configured family, contaminating telemetry datasets and potentially disclosing flow metadata to an unintended destination.

**Fix direction:** Preserve family in `CollectorConfig`; group by `(template, family)` or split collectors before template grouping; gate each group while sharing the per-instance sampling result. Add v9 and IPFIX mixed-family wire tests for shared and distinct templates.

**Labels:** `flowexport`, `netflow-v9`, `ipfix`, `sampling`, `address-family`, `collector-routing`

**Dedup note:** Closed #2462 was cross-instance collector flattening. No supplied open issue owns within-one-instance family cross-fanout.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

## R73

**Title:** Lenient source-NAT aggregate loading can expand and allocate multi-gigabyte per-address port bitmaps

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence with snippets:** The strict aggregate gate defines 1,048,576 addresses and `2^33` port slots, with exact saturating arithmetic, at `pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_nat.go:2320-2522`. Its call site explicitly downgrades failure on the tolerant path (`pkg/config/compiler_uniformgates_nat.go:208-235`):

```go
if err := validateSourceNATAggregateCardinalityStrict(cfg); err != nil {
    if opts.lenientDestNATAddresses {
        cfg.Warnings = append(cfg.Warnings, ...)
    } else { return err }
}
```

`Store.Load` invokes `compileTreeLenient` (`pkg/configstore/store_persist.go:79-82`), and `Store.SyncApply` does so at `pkg/configstore/store.go:630-688` before promoting `s.active/s.compiled`. The Go snapshot keeps compact prefix strings, not expanded addresses (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_source.go:75-86`, `:177-200`). Rust permits each individual `/16` and expands it fully (`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:470-513`). It then constructs an allocator before checking reuse (`:723-735`):

```rust
if total_pool > 0 {
    rule.pool_allocator = PortAllocator::new(total_pool, port_low, port_high);
}
if let Some(key) = rule.allocator_key() {
    if let Some(existing) = pool_allocators.get(&key) {
        rule.pool_allocator = existing.clone();
    }
    ...
}
```

`PortAllocator::new` builds one `AddressOccupancy` per address (`userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs:771-800`), and each occupancy pushes `ceil(range/64)` `AtomicU64`s (`:521-535`). There is no aggregate Rust boundary cap and this path returns `Vec`, not `Result`.

**Trace:** An old persisted config or HA peer supplies three referenced `/16` source-NAT pools with default ports. Lenient compilation computes the over-budget aggregate, warns, and retains the config. Go emits three compact `/16` strings across the relevant rule snapshots. Manager `ApplyConfig` builds and publishes the snapshot (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:205-217`, `:315-354`). Rust forwarding build calls `parse_source_nat_rules_with_previous` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding_build/mod.rs:300-316`), expands 196,608 concrete addresses, then eagerly allocates occupancy before allocator reuse selection. If memory is available, the state can publish; if allocation exhausts memory, there is no structured integrity error to trigger the normal previous-good path.

**Refutation attempt:** I independently checked all requested boundaries:

- **Arithmetic:** `3 * 65,536 = 196,608` addresses; default range `65,535 - 1,024 + 1 = 64,512`; slots/bits `196,608 * 64,512 = 12,683,575,296`; occupancy bytes `/8 = 1,585,446,912`, exactly `1.4765625 GiB`, before address vectors, counters, occupancy structs, recycle mutex/deques, and live-state vectors.
- **Allocation order:** address expansion precedes `PortAllocator::new`; bitmap construction precedes both same-build `pool_allocators` reuse and `previous_allocators` reuse. Reuse can discard a newly built allocator but cannot prevent its transient allocation. A helper cold start has no previous allocator.
- **Real reachability:** `Store.Load` and `SyncApply` use lenient compilation; the latter promotes active before daemon apply. The Go manager sends the retained pool prefixes to the Rust apply handler. This is userspace dataplane code, not retired eBPF/DPDK logic.
- **Snapshot poisoning/last-good:** Rust same-plan refresh and reconcile build before publishing and retain the old Rust snapshot on ordinary `Err` (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:273-300`; handler `server/handlers/snapshot.rs:250-284`, `:397-421`). Allocation is infallible at the API level; OOM abort/panic cannot return that `Err`. The Rust persisted snapshot is not intentionally advanced before a failed build, but Go `Load` already treats the persisted config as active and `SyncApply` promotes it before apply, so restart/reapply can repeatedly re-enter the allocation. Last-good protects structured integrity failures, not process memory exhaustion.
- **Last-boundary caps:** Rust caps each member at 65,536 hosts, so each `/16` is valid. No sum-of-members, sum-of-rules, or sum-of-port-slots cap exists after the tolerant Go warning. `MAX_SOURCE_NAT_POOL_TRACKED_FLOWS` caps flow-map entries, not occupancy bitmap construction.
- **Pool-unusable and reuse:** `total_pool > 0` allocation is outside `pool_failure` checks, so even a separately marked unusable pool can allocate if addresses expanded. Reuse lookup occurs only after construction.
- **Tests:** Strict tests pin rejection of three full-range `/16`s and lenient warning behavior, but no test drives that exact lenient config through Rust because doing so would allocate about 1.5 GB.

**HPC/invariant check:** Resource admission must be enforced at the final allocation boundary, independent of Go strict/lenient policy and wire provenance. Counting compact prefixes is O(number of members); allocator memory must be bounded before expansion/bitmap construction. Reuse lookup should precede fresh allocation.

**Why it matters:** Boot, HA convergence, or helper apply can stall or terminate the userspace dataplane under a config the tolerant control-plane path intentionally accepts. The affected allocation is on a security-critical snapshot path and can recur after restart.

**Fix direction:** Add a Rust checked aggregate budget over all source-NAT snapshots before expansion, returning `SnapshotIntegrityError`; move allocator-key/previous reuse lookup before fresh construction; consider lazy/chunked occupancy allocation so capacity is proportional to used addresses/ports. On the Go side, define an explicit lenient quarantine/fail-closed representation instead of warning and emitting an unsafe pool.

**Labels:** `config`, `configstore`, `userspace-dp`, `source-nat`, `allocator`, `oom`, `lenient-load`, `ha-sync`, `resource-bound`

**Dedup note:** The complete open issue corpus and dedup index contain related allocator architecture and source-NAT correctness items, but no issue owns the exact warning-only aggregate gate followed by Rust expansion/eager bitmap allocation. Internal `#5877` is provenance for the strict gate, not an open owner of this tolerant-load residual.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

Similar titles were not treated as ownership without the same cause and remediation.

## R01 - MATERIAL

**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High.

**Final anchors:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:194`, `:198`, `:246`, `:265`, `:304`, `:338`; `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:406`, `:435`; `userspace-dp/src/session/expire.rs:342`; `userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:1226`, `:1247`; `userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:825`, `:838`, `:963`.

**Trace and guards:** `dnat_v4_key_bytes`/the IPv6 equivalent key only protocol, translated address, and translated port. Interface SNAT changes only the address, so different remote flows can share the marker. Publish uses `BPF_ANY`; every forward close delta unconditionally calls `bpf_map_delete_elem`. The live userspace-XDP native-GRE classifier consumes only marker presence for embedded ICMP steering. Exact session lookup protects normal replies but cannot replace this embedded-packet marker. This is a live userspace shim path, not the retired eBPF forwarding pipeline.

**Validation:** `cargo test close_delta_deletes_dnat_table_entry_for_snat_flow -- --test-threads=1` passed (1/1). It confirms every SNAT close attempts deletion; it has no two-holder lifetime case and therefore supports rather than falsifies the root.

**Dedup and rationale:** No final open issue owns the steering-map lifetime. #6522 is a source-NAT allocator holder-release defect leading to pool-port reuse; #6218 contains PMTUD/robustness cohort items but not this map key. Historical #2979 fixed the opposite leak by adding the unconditional delete, while #4399/#4438 address Rust session-index collisions. The resource, consumer, consequence, and fix differ. **Fix direction:** maintain coordinator-side holders/refcounts per steering key, publish on `0 -> 1`, delete on `1 -> 0`, include HA imports/resync, and preserve static-DNAT ownership; alternatively redesign the map identity without losing embedded-ICMP lookup capability.

## R02 - MATERIAL

**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High.

**Final anchors:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/ha_state.rs:36`; `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/ha.rs:66`, `:80`, `:101`; `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/nat.rs:137`; `userspace-dp/src/server/lifecycle.rs:184`, `:199`; `userspace-dp/src/server/helpers/status.rs:274`; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:369`, `:383`, `:408`; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:391`, `:438`, `:486`; `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:26`, `:37`, `:277`; `pkg/daemon/cluster_topology_preflight.go:84`; `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_dataplane.go:137`; `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:221`.

**Trace and guards:** The report's literal cold-helper trace is falsified: Rust starts with `forwarding_armed=false`, snapshot application remains disarmed, and Go sends HA state before `syncDesiredForwardingStateLocked` can arm. #5840's preflight also rejects live standalone/cluster mode flips. The root is nevertheless production-reachable through a supported intra-cluster edit. A cluster with zero redundancy groups is valid; `syncHAStateLocked` sends nothing when the inventory is empty, leaving the worker map empty. On a later zero-RG to first-RG commit, the topology preflight returns success because runtime and desired mode are both clustered. The already-armed helper receives the new forwarding snapshot and `applyHelperStatusLocked` before HA publication; daemon step 2 applies the dataplane before step 19 updates the cluster state machine. During that interval, an RG-owned interface-NAT `LocalDelivery` reaches the explicit `ha_state.is_empty()` permit and bypasses owner lookup. `rgTransitionInFlight` only fences explicit activation callbacks, not this config-apply ordering.

**Validation:** `go test ./pkg/daemon -run '^TestClusterTopologyDay2TransitionRejected$' -count=1` passed and proves only cross-mode transitions are rejected. `go test ./pkg/config -run '^TestChassisRedundancyGroupInRangeCommits$' -count=1` passed; its control explicitly accepts a cluster with no RG stanza, confirming the alternate starting state. The cold-start refutation therefore narrows but does not eliminate the root.

**Dedup and rationale:** #6187 owns a future live standalone/cluster supervisor and the current restart boundary; it does not own intra-cluster RG-inventory publication ordering. #6707 concerns rejected policy snapshots, not an accepted snapshot observed against an uninitialized HA inventory. None owns their mixed-timeout interaction. **Fix direction:** track compact flow-level handshake state and keep both directions in the opening class until the final ACK; at minimum, forbid companion extension while handshake completion is false and use the shorter effective deadline.

## R13 / M14 - MATERIAL

- **Severity / confidence:** Medium / High.
- **Final line anchors:** `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:248-301`, `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:356-379`, `pkg/dhcp/dhcpv4.go:396-454`, `go.mod:9`; pinned dependency `dhcpv4/dhcpv4.go:608-617` and `dhcpv4/options.go:69-76`.
- **Trace:** A network DHCP ACK reaches `doDHCPv4`, then `leaseFromACKv4`. `classlessStaticRoutes` calls the dependency's decoded option-121 accessor. That accessor returns nil both when the option is absent and when `Routes.FromBytes` fails. The local helper also tests option 249 with `len(raw) > 0`, then returns `present=false` when no decoded routes remain. `leaseFromACKv4` consequently enters the option-3 `Router()` branch and commits that gateway. `Options.Has` exists in the pinned dependency, but the path does not use it.
- **Refutation and checks:** The positive controls `TestLeaseFromACKv4ClasslessRoutesSupersedeOption3`, `TestLeaseFromACKv4ClasslessOnlySpecificNoDefault`, and `TestClasslessStaticRoutesEncoding` pass. They prove valid decoded routes and valid no-default precedence, but do not exercise an empty or malformed present option. The decoder source directly refutes the theory that decode failure preserves presence.
- **Dedup/materiality rationale:** Closed #4118 added valid RFC 3442 support and valid-option precedence; it did not own the current presence/decode-error collapse or its fail-closed remediation. An accepted ACK can therefore install a server-supplied option-3 default that RFC 3442 presence should suppress. The result is wrong uplink routing until lease replacement, which clears the materiality gate at Medium.
- **MATERIAL fix direction:** Inspect option presence before decoding (`Options.Has`), preserve option-121 precedence over 249 and option 3, and propagate malformed data as a lease error or as present-but-unusable that suppresses option 3. Add empty and malformed 121/249 tests, including malformed 121 plus valid 249/3, at acquire, renew, and rebind parsing.

## R14 / M15 - MATERIAL

- **Severity / confidence:** High / High.
- **Final line anchors:** `pkg/dhcpserver/lease_lfc.go:3-80`, `pkg/dhcpserver/ddns_leases.go:163-200`, `pkg/dhcpserver/ddns.go:45-90`, `pkg/ddns/manager.go:942-984`, `pkg/ddns/manager.go:1290-1371`, `pkg/dhcpserver/lease_source_5938_test.go:172-227`.
- **Trace:** Production DDNS uses `keaLeaseParser`, which reads only `.2`, `.1`, and current. During LFC, Kea renames the completed output to the finish file, removes previous and input, and then renames finish to previous. A crash in that interval can leave a full `.completed`, no `.1`/`.2`, and a fresh header-only current. The parser validates those available files and returns `(nil, nil)` as trusted-empty. DDNS marks no family untrusted, constructs an empty desired set, and Pass 1 deletes every owned A/AAAA/PTR record in the admitted scopes.
- **High-candidate falsification:** The in-tree safety claim says `.completed` is a zero-content marker (`lease_lfc.go:50-58`) and the regression test creates it empty (`lease_source_5938_test.go:207`). The official [Kea LFC process contract](https://kea.readthedocs.io/en/kea-2.7.0/arm/lfc.html) says output is moved to finish after writing and finish is later moved to previous, so finish contains the completed lease output. This disproves the premise rather than merely exposing an untested branch. The selected LFC tests all pass and therefore pin the incorrect premise.
- **Dedup/materiality rationale:** Closed #5796/#5938 own the earlier current-only read and crash-safety attempt, but their documented invariant is factually incomplete; no open body owns finish-file generation selection and destructive-DDNS gating. A single ordinary LFC interruption can trigger bulk authoritative-record withdrawal, so High survives.
- **MATERIAL fix direction:** Model the Kea file-set phases explicitly. When finish exists, treat its completed rows as the compacted baseline and merge newer current rows; take a stable before/after file-set snapshot and retry on rotation. Any inconsistent or unreadable phase must mark the family untrusted for destructive DDNS. Add crash-point tests for every rename/delete phase with real lease-bearing `.completed` content.

## Root findings

### R37 / M38

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_read.go:298-330`,
`pkg/cluster/sync.go:847-857`, `pkg/cluster/sync_conn_config.go:312-395`, and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:474-497`.

**Trace and reachability:** The receiver decodes a config update and advances
`lastRecvConfigGen` at `sync_conn_read.go:304-314` before attempting the
nonblocking send to the 64-entry apply channel. A full channel takes the `default`
case, discarding the only payload while retaining the advanced generation. The
ordered consumer in `sync_conn_config.go:312-395` is the sole route to apply and to
`noteConfigApplyFailure`; a dropped payload reaches neither. On the sender,
`daemon_ha_sync.go:474-497` claims the stable `(connection epoch, generation)`
marker before `QueueConfig`, so subsequent periodic checks do not retransmit that
generation. This is a live HA config-sync path, not retired code.

**Falsification:** The focused single-push and apply-failure tests passed. They
cover accepted delivery and consumer-reported failure, but do not fill the receive
queue. The queue-full branch still has no durable latest-value slot, NACK, sender
acknowledgement, retry debt, or health downgrade. The standby can therefore remain
stale without the normal apply-failure accounting.

**Dedup/materiality:** No final open issue owns this cause and remediation. #5084
concerns an epoch race on queued config, while #6173 concerns advertised heartbeat
generation. Neither covers receiver-side queue overflow after high-water advance
and sender-side one-shot suppression. This can leave a standby stale for an
unexpected failover, so it passes the materiality gate.

**Fix direction:** Make generation advancement conditional on durable acceptance,
or replace the lossy queue edge with a durable latest-generation slot. Add an
explicit receiver acknowledgement/NACK and retry or debt propagation so the sender
does not permanently claim an unaccepted generation. Add a queue-saturation test.

### R38 / M39

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** High / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:211-238`,
`pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:290-301`, `pkg/vrrp/packet.go:19-32`,
`pkg/vrrp/packet.go:56-64`, `pkg/vrrp/instance_send.go:38-86`,
`pkg/vrrp/instance_send.go:177-198`, `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1296-1342`, and
`pkg/vrrp/manager.go:443-490`.

**Trace and reachability:** Config accepts an unbounded number of virtual addresses,
and both address collectors copy all of them into live VRRP instances. Packet
serialization supports at most 255 addresses. IPv6 also prepends the link-local
address, so 255 configured addresses become 256. `sendAdvert` logs and discards
serialization/send errors. During MASTER transition, the instance first installs
VIPs, then calls the void sender, emits the event/GARP path, and returns success.
Manager validation checks family, VRID, and duplicate domains but not cardinality.

**Falsification:** `TestMarshal_RejectsOver255Addresses` and boundary tests passed,
confirming that the serializer rejects the oversized packet. They also confirm the
failure is not prevented upstream. No caller observes that rejection or rolls back
ownership. The node can own service addresses while sending no usable adverts,
which creates a split-brain window.

**Dedup/materiality:** Full issue-body search found no issue covering unbounded
VRRP address cardinality plus ignored advert failure. This is reachable through
accepted configuration and controls ownership, so it is material and not cohort
noise.

**Fix direction:** Enforce per-family cardinality during strict validation, with a
configured IPv6 maximum of 254 when the link-local address is prepended. Repeat the
guard in runtime construction and make advertisement failure gate or roll back
MASTER ownership. Add transition tests at 255/256 effective addresses.

### R39 / M40

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/config/interfaces_iter.go:5-14`,
`pkg/config/compiler_validate_warn.go:819-823`, `pkg/config/types.go:62-74`,
`pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:154-175`, `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:203-225`,
`pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:255-294`, `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:42-55`, and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:81-97,210-235`.

**Trace and reachability:** The config package explicitly tolerates present-but-nil
interface and unit map entries on lenient load and HA sync, and warning validation
tolerates nil redundancy groups. `RethToPhysical` is nil-safe, but the live VRRP
collectors are not: they dereference nil redundancy groups, interfaces, or units.
Cluster apply calls `CollectRethInstances` before manager reconciliation; direct
election readiness and address actions call `RethVIPsForRG`. Thus both ownership
modes can panic on data the compatibility path intentionally admits.

**Falsification:** The production callers were followed past iteration to the
unguarded dereferences; there is no earlier strict validator on peer-applied or
leniently loaded state. This is not a retired helper. Existing tests do not inject
nil slots through both ownership modes.

**Dedup/materiality:** Historical #3501 added the sibling nil guard in
`RethToPhysical`; it did not change these collectors. No open issue owns the
remaining production panic. A peer-provided or retained compatible config can
abort reconciliation, so the root is material.

**Fix direction:** Use the nil-safe range helpers consistently, skip nil redundancy
groups, interfaces, and units before dereference, and add lenient-load/HA-sync tests
for both VRRP and direct-election collectors.

### R40 / M41

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/config/schema_interfaces.go:36,83-85`,
`pkg/config/compiler_interfaces.go:136-142`,
`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_reth_vrrp.go:50-87`,
`pkg/config/compiler_system.go:1897-1901`, `pkg/vrrp/vrrp.go:169-189`,

**Trace and reachability:** The wildcard interface schema permits

any positive-group interface and falls back to the interface itself as the physical
name. Direct-election VIP collection, which is enabled by default, excludes
non-`reth` interfaces. Independently, networkd compilation treats any positive
group as VRRP-owned and replaces its actual addresses with link-local configuration.
The default direct mode therefore suppresses static addresses but never installs
them through its owner; toggling the mode changes semantics.

**Falsification:** Default-election and valid-RETH tests passed, but neither tests a

**Dedup/materiality:** No final issue body covers this cross-layer predicate split.
The accepted configuration can remove addresses from an ordinary interface in the
default mode, which is a concrete outage rather than a low-value validation cohort.

**Fix direction:** Add contextual strict validation that limits the option to RETH
interfaces and make tolerant handling fail closed. Share one RETH ownership
predicate between networkd generation and both owner implementations, with mode
parity tests.

no such inventory; that remediation cannot discover inherited pinned entries. No
other final issue owns restart reconstruction, so the root is material.

**Fix direction:** While control is disabled, perform a one-time authoritative
classifier-map sweep/recreate or reconstruct inventory from pinned maps before any
enable. Separate classifier pin lifecycle from intentionally retained session maps,
and test a new manager against stale prepopulated pins.

### R44 / M45

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** Medium / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/mod.rs:91-96`,
`userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/sync_session.rs:9-42`,
`userspace-dp/src/session_import.rs:39-42`,
`userspace-dp/src/session_import.rs:67-121`,
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/process_control.go:181-216`,
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:1112-1167`,
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:1265-1303`,
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:391-447`, and
`pkg/cluster/sync_conn_gen.go:435-491`.

**Trace and reachability:** The Rust response defaults to `ok=true`. The sync-session
handler invokes a void import method, so it retains that success even when the
aggregate session ceiling branch increments a drop counter and returns before
publishing the session. Go treats only an explicit false response as failure. Its
HA path has already written the BPF mirror before RPC; the apparent success clears
mirror-failure state, records installed generation/stats, and leaves takeover
readiness ungated despite the userspace session being absent.

**Falsification:** The focused Rust ceiling test passed, proving the import is
intentionally rejected and does not fan out. It also isolates the missing contract:
the handler has no return value with which to change its default success. No later
Go validator confirms userspace publication.

**Dedup/materiality:** The named POSSIBLE_EXISTING issue #6600 was inspected in
full. It covers publication before a later worker NAT-port reservation can race or
fail. R44 rejects before publication at the aggregate ceiling while the handler
still returns success. Reservation-before-publish or worker-failure propagation
does not repair this capacity-result contract. No final issue owns it.

**Fix direction:** Return a typed import result such as inserted, replaced,
rejected-capacity, or stale. Map semantic rejection to `ok=false`; have Go restore
or invalidate the BPF mirror and retain health debt. Test the cap response, mirror
rollback, generation accounting, and takeover gate together.

### R45 / M46

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** P1 / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/devicemap/devicemap.go:98-176`,
`pkg/devicemap/devicemap.go:280-315`, `pkg/devicemap/devicemap_test.go:27-53`,
`pkg/daemon/device_map.go:95-106`, `pkg/daemon/device_map.go:161-227`,
`pkg/daemon/device_map.go:492-540`, and
`pkg/grpcapi/server_show_device_map.go:26-76`.

**Trace and reachability:** Sysfs enumeration calls `netlink.LinkByName` per NIC but
silently ignores its error and appends a partial observation with no permanent MAC.
The resolver checks a MAC mismatch only when that field is non-empty; an empty value
falls through to PCI-only binding. Startup treats any resulting Bound entry as
rename-eligible. Commit preflight fails only a whole enumeration error, which the
per-NIC collapse suppresses, and the show command reports `(none)` rather than
uncertainty. A transient identity-read failure on replacement hardware at a pinned
PCI address can therefore bypass the dual-identity mismatch and durably rename the
wrong management or zone interface.

**Falsification:** The three focused resolver tests passed: matching PCI+MAC binds,
mismatched MAC refuses, and PCI-only with empty permanent MAC succeeds. The last
test confirms the unsafe fallback after the observation error has been collapsed.
The live startup, preflight, rename, and diagnostic callers contain no compensating
guard.

**Dedup/materiality:** #6546 concerns duplicate logical device-map entries; #6678
concerns `OriginalName` fallback; #5842 concerns later write/rename/reload failure;
and #1958 is a broad binding architecture umbrella. None owns the specific lost
netlink observation error or requires blocking PCI-only mutation when identity is
unknown. Because this can rename the management NIC on replacement hardware, it is
P1 and material.

**Fix direction:** Return a typed per-NIC observation result that distinguishes
hardware without a permanent-MAC attribute from a failed read. Abort commit,
startup mutation, and rename for mapped/protected interfaces with incomplete
identity, and expose uncertainty in diagnostics. Add injected LinkByName-failure
tests asserting zero rename side effects.

### R46 / M47

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** High / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:25-64`,
`pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:150-205`, `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:290-348`,
`pkg/vrrp/instance.go:989-1003`, `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:1365-1379`,
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1244-1287`,
`pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:126-132`,
`pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:239-253`,
`pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:294-395`, and
`pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver_test.go:67-89`.

**Trace and reachability:** Shutdown cancels and drains ordinary apply work, then
withdraws HA state and stops VRRP, but never calls the DHCP-server manager. VRRP
stop sends a priority-zero advert and removes VIPs without emitting the BACKUP
event; only that event callback enqueues `ApplyAsync(nil)` for Kea. The DHCP manager
is authoritative over external systemd units, `Apply(nil)` is its stop operation,
and its worker has no independent Close/Stop lifecycle. Routine shutdown of an
active owner can therefore leave Kea serving after ownership withdrawal and permit
dual DHCP service when the peer takes over.

**Falsification:** `TestApplyNilStopsStaleActiveUnits` passed, confirming the missing
operation would stop stale units. VRRP shutdown/event and daemon shutdown tests
passed their narrower contracts, but no shutdown path invokes or drains that
operation. Source search found no alternative production stop call.

**Dedup/materiality:** The named POSSIBLE_EXISTING issue #6535 was inspected in
full. It covers retry debt after an existing Kea apply fails and proposes a periodic
desired-versus-applied converger. R46 creates no stop request after shutdown has
canceled/joined the converger; a periodic retry cannot invent shutdown desired=nil
or run after teardown. No final issue owns lifecycle quiescence before ownership
withdrawal.

**Fix direction:** Add a synchronous, newest-generation DHCP-server
`StopAndDrain`/`Apply(nil)` before priority-zero withdrawal and heartbeat shutdown.
It must supersede queued MASTER applies and report bounded failure. Test active
shutdown ordering and peer takeover with an external-unit fake.

### R47 / M48

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** High / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:38-72`,
`pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:25-64`, `pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:253-312`,
`pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:423-446`, `pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:500-512`, and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:73-114`.

**Trace and reachability:** Both the apply semaphore acquisition and the full apply
pipeline use `context.Background`. The daemon performs one apply drain early in
shutdown, but the DHCP client's process-lifetime context and renewal timer
deliberately survive that drain. `StopAll` can cancel the timer, yet production
shutdown never calls it. A timer armed before the drain can fire afterward; its
callback reads config and starts a new non-cancellable full apply while FRR, VRRP,
cluster, and dataplane teardown is underway.

**Falsification:** Focused lease-change/timer behavior and bounded HA-shutdown tests
passed. They do not arm a renewal across the final drain. Source search confirmed
there is no daemon-side `d.dhcp.StopAll` or equivalent quiesce call and no lifecycle
generation check at the callback or apply entry.

**Dedup/materiality:** #6716 concerns a stale active-config snapshot taken before
waiting on the semaphore, not creation of a new apply after the shutdown drain.
Historical #3758 concerned a different ip-monitor `Background` shutdown blocker.
Neither remediation closes this timer lifecycle. Concurrent full apply during
teardown can restore state after withdrawal or touch stopped subsystems, so it is
material.

**Fix direction:** Add a shutdown quiesce operation that stops renewal timers,
rejects new callbacks, and joins in-flight DHCP callback work while preserving
leases, then perform the final apply drain. Gate every background apply on daemon
lifecycle/generation and add a deterministic post-drain timer test.

### R48 / M49

**Final classification:** MATERIAL  
**Severity / confidence:** High / High

**Final-SHA anchors:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_naming.go:77-85`,
`pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:838-907`, `pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:914-956`,
`pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:974-1014`, and
`pkg/daemon/linksetup.go:493-526`.

**Trace and reachability:** Bootstrap invokes the lifeline migration on the live
naming path. Snapshot collection converts `LinkByName` failure to an empty tuple,
discards `AddrList` error, and continues after `RouteList` errors. The writer then
interprets missing IPv4/IPv6 state or existing DHCP as `DHCP=yes`. It writes the
snapshot and link files and performs a down/rename/up cycle followed by reload,
even though an incomplete observation can have fabricated DHCP mode or omitted the
gateway. A transient netlink failure can therefore replace a working static
management lifeline and cycle the interface into lockout.

**Falsification:** The exact bootstrap caller, observation helpers, writer, and
rename implementation were traced. No typed completeness result or pre-mutation
guard exists. A minimal fault-injection probe was not practical without modifying
source because the netlink calls are hard-coded; existing bootstrap tests do not
exercise these errors. The static side-effect ordering is unambiguous.

**Dedup/materiality:** #5842 covers failures during the later file write,
rename, and reload steps, not observation errors being laundered into a successful
DHCP snapshot. #1958 is a broad architecture issue and does not prescribe atomic
snapshot validity. No final issue owns the cause and required no-side-effect guard.

**Fix direction:** Return a typed complete/incomplete snapshot and propagate every
link, address, and route observation error. Abort before all writes, renames, and
reloads unless the snapshot is complete. Introduce injectable netlink seams and
tests asserting zero side effects for each observation failure.

## Final disposition

All twelve roots survive the retired-path, cross-report collapse,
materiality/cohort, and fresh 290-body dedup gates. Each has one final classification:
MATERIAL. No assigned root is owned by an existing final open issue, fixed at the
immutable tip, stale, or merely cohort-level.

## High Confidence Findings

### F1

Title: Per-session close deletes a shared reverse-NAT steering key

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence:

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:198` derives the BPF key from only protocol, translated address, and translated port. It contains neither the original endpoint nor the remote endpoint:

```rust

    dk[0] = key.protocol;
    dk[4..8].copy_from_slice(&snat_v4.octets());

```

`userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs:1247` confirms live interface SNAT changes only the address and leaves `rewrite_src_port` at its default `None`, so independent flows retaining the same source port can share that key:

```rust
            return SourceNatLookup::Matched(NatDecision {
                rewrite_src: Some(rewrite_src),
                rewrite_dst: None,
                ..NatDecision::default()
            });
```

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:338` overwrites an existing same-key marker rather than acquiring distinguishable ownership:

```rust

                libbpf_sys::bpf_map_update_elem(

                    dk.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>(),
                    dv.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>(),
                    libbpf_sys::BPF_ANY as u64,

```

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/checksum.rs:259` then unconditionally deletes that shared key. There is no holder count, value/flag check, or compare-before-delete:

```rust

            // without a real BPF map (unprivileged_bpf_disabled blocks map
            // creation under `cargo test`). Production cost is one relaxed
            // increment under `#[cfg(test)]` only.
            #[cfg(test)]
            DNAT_DELETE_ATTEMPTS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
            unsafe {
                libbpf_sys::bpf_map_delete_elem(fd, dk.as_ptr().cast::<libc::c_void>());
            }
```

`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/session_delta.rs:427` invokes that deletion for every forward SNAT close delta:

```rust
            // #2979: delete the dynamic reverse-NAT dnat_table entry this
            // SNAT'd session published at install. Keyed on the SAME forward
            // key + nat decision used by publish_dnat_table_entry (the Close
            // delta carries the forward key — it is gated on !is_reverse at
            // construction in session/expire.rs and session/mod.rs). A
            // non-SNAT session is a no-op (no rewrite_src -> no key). Only the
            // forward key publishes a dnat_table entry, so it is NOT repeated
            // for the reverse key below.
            super::checksum::delete_dnat_table_entry(dnat_fds, &delta.key, delta.decision.nat);
```

`userspace-xdp/src/lib.rs:831` is the live consumer: when no exact session marker exists for an embedded/reply packet, native-GRE steering depends only on presence of this DNAT key:

```rust
    // as the port key, so native GRE must use the same field here or the first
    // reply falls through to the kernel path.
    let dnat_port = if protocol == PROTO_ICMP {
        key.src_port
    } else {
        key.dst_port
    };
    if dnat_lookup_v4(protocol, dst_v4, dnat_port).is_some() {
        return USERSPACE_SESSION_ACTION_REDIRECT;
```

Trace:

1. Two interface-SNAT sessions use the same protocol, egress address, and preserved source port but different remote endpoints. Both are legal: the full reverse session index can distinguish the remote endpoint, while interface mode has no port allocator reservation.
2. Each install publishes the same `dnat_table` key with `BPF_ANY`; because the XDP consumer tests only `.is_some()`, the single value acts as a shared steering marker.
3. Either session closes or expires. Its forward Close delta reaches `delete_dnat_table_entry`, which deletes the one map element without checking for another live holder.
4. The sibling session remains live. Ordinary exact replies can still hit `USERSPACE_SESSIONS`, but an inbound native-GRE embedded ICMP error has no exact session of its own and relies on `dnat_lookup_v4`/`dnat_lookup_v6` to enter userspace.
5. The lookup now misses, the packet falls away from the userspace embedded-ICMP reverse-NAT path, and PMTUD/traceroute feedback for the surviving flow is lost. The IPv6 helper has the same key lifetime defect.

Refutation attempt:

I checked both source-NAT collision controls and the live classifier. Pool address-only reservations reject duplicate full reverse identities, but explicitly allow a different remote endpoint while the BPF key omits that endpoint; interface SNAT does not reserve a translated port at all. I also checked whether exact session steering makes the marker redundant: it covers normal replies, not the embedded ICMP packet described by the live `userspace-xdp` comments and lookup. Finally, I excluded the retired eBPF dataplane; this finding survives because the Rust userspace-XDP program reads the map in the live native-GRE path.

HPC/invariant check:

The unsafe map syscall buffers have the correct fixed size and the native/network byte order matches the reader. The broken invariant is lifetime ownership: `one map key exists iff at least one live session needs steering`, while the code implements last-writer/first-closer semantics. No packet-path allocation is introduced by the bug; repair must avoid adding a contended RMW to every packet. Session install/close is the appropriate control point.

Why it matters:

A short-lived flow can remove steering needed by an unrelated live flow. On native GRE, loss of ICMP Too-Big/Packet-Too-Big feedback creates a PMTUD blackhole and large TCP transfers can stall; traceroute and other embedded-ICMP diagnostics also fail. This is live userspace behavior, not retired eBPF residue.

Fix direction:

Give the steering key explicit multi-holder ownership. The coordinator already serializes session deltas, so maintain a per-key holder count (including HA-imported sessions), publish on `0 -> 1`, and delete only on `1 -> 0`; reconcile counts on loss-of-sync. Alternatively change the map schema/lookup to include enough remote identity to make keys unique, but that must still support embedded ICMP parsing. Add v4/v6 regressions with two same-port interface/address-only SNAT flows to different remotes: closing either one must leave the marker until the last holder closes. Also protect static-DNAT keys from dynamic ownership transitions.
