# opus-001 A7 batch 1 Linux networking/host-integration review

## Review envelope

- Role: Linux networking/host-integration reviewer for daemon lifecycle, systemd/networkd/netlink ownership, FRR/strongSwan execution, route/VRF correctness, apply/teardown ordering, retries, races/resources, cold boot, vSRX compatibility, performance, modularity, and tests.
- Detached review worktree: `/tmp/review-wt-opus-001-A7-b1` at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`, created before any source read.
- Setup-tip verification: after a fresh `git fetch origin master`, `HEAD`, the requested setup tip, and `origin/master` all resolved to `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.
- Assigned scope: 150/150 files and 46,694/46,694 lines under `pkg/daemon`: 55 production files (27,725 lines) and 95 test files (18,969 lines).
- Required orientation read: worktree deep-review skill, scratch orientation, all 722 current dedup-index rows, and the complete A7-b1 assignment.
- Outside reads were narrow and trace-driven: DHCP client/server/relay lifecycle, VRRP manager stop semantics, RA manager/sender lifecycle, LLDP manager apply semantics, userspace filter nil-shape behavior, strict filter-reference validation, config-store tolerant-load comments, and the Rust AF_XDP bind owner. No unrelated implementation was reviewed.
- Live-path rule: Go plus Rust AF_XDP/userspace behavior was reviewed as current. Retired eBPF/DPDK references were classified only as STALE and did not produce a live finding.
- Validation: `go test ./pkg/daemon -count=1` passed in 16.703s; `go test -race ./pkg/daemon -count=1` passed in 36.185s.
- Result: 9 MATERIAL findings: 5 High and 4 Medium. No Critical, COHORT, or independently fileable Low finding survived refutation.

## Findings

### A7-b1-01

Title: Orderly HA shutdown relinquishes ownership without stopping the authoritative Kea units

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:196-205` removes VRRP ownership and heartbeat without issuing any DHCP-server clear:

> 196 `// Stop VRRP manager (removes VIPs, sends priority-0).`
> 197 `if d.vrrpMgr != nil {`
> 198 `    d.vrrpMgr.Stop()`
> 199 `}`
> 200 ``
> 201 `// Stop cluster monitor (heartbeats) immediately after VRRP priority-0.`
> 202 `// This ensures the peer's heartbeat timeout starts promptly instead of`
> 203 `// being delayed by the 5s sync Stop timeout below.`
> 204 `if d.cluster != nil {`
> 205 `    d.cluster.Stop()`

The only authoritative demotion clear is `d.dhcpServer.ApplyAsync(nil, ...)` in the VRRP BACKUP callback at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:1273-1287`. `pkg/vrrp/manager.go:328-343` explicitly says the stop arm does not emit an event before closing `eventCh`. Kea is external state: `pkg/dhcpserver/dhcpserver.go:126-132,239-253,294-320` owns systemd units and defines `Apply(nil)` as the operation that stops an active unit regardless of which xpfd instance started it.

Trace: Start with this node MASTER for a DHCP-serving RG and Kea active. SIGTERM enters `shutdown`, drains only the current config apply, withdraws RAs/VIPs, sends VRRP priority zero, and stops cluster heartbeat. `vrrpMgr.Stop` intentionally emits no BACKUP event, so `clearRethServicesForRG` never enqueues the nil desired state. xpfd then exits while the independent `kea-dhcp4-server`/`kea-dhcp6-server` systemd unit continues serving the old interfaces. The peer promotes and starts its own Kea generation. Both nodes can answer the same client segment after ownership has transferred.

Refutation attempt: I searched the complete shutdown path and all DHCP references in `daemon_run.go`/`daemon_run_shutdown.go`; there is no synchronous clear, async clear, worker drain, or unit stop. Process exit cannot stop a systemd-managed unit. The manager's generation ordering would make a late synchronous `Apply(nil)` authoritative, but shutdown never calls it. Preserving DHCP client addresses across graceful restart is documented separately and does not justify preserving an HA-gated DHCP server after VRRP relinquishment. This is High rather than Critical because it requires cluster DHCP service plus an orderly stop of an active owner.

HPC/invariant check: Cold lifecycle invariant violated: before an HA node publishes or signals loss of RG ownership, every externally persistent service able to answer for that RG must be synchronously quiesced. Kea must be inactive before priority-zero/heartbeat relinquishment can let the peer serve.

Why it matters: A routine package restart or administrative stop can create persistent dual DHCP, duplicate offers/ACKs, conflicting lease ownership, and client address instability even though VRRP and status correctly show only the peer as owner.

Fix direction: Add a bounded `StopAndDrain`/synchronous newest-generation `Apply(nil)` for cluster Kea before VRRP ownership is relinquished. It must supersede pending MASTER work and report a stop failure through shutdown health/logging. Add RETH and direct-ownership shutdown-order tests proving Kea is inactive before priority zero and that a queued MASTER apply cannot run afterward.

Labels: MATERIAL, daemon-lifecycle, HA, DHCP, Kea, systemd, shutdown-order, dual-service, userspace-live

Dedup note: Open GH #6535 matches `dhcpServer.ApplyAsync` plus lost transition retry debt plus persistent dual DHCP after a failed apply. This finding is a different mechanism at `Daemon.shutdown`/`vrrp.Manager.Stop`: no BACKUP transition and therefore no stop request exists. Closed #1778 made `Apply(nil)` authoritative over stale systemd units, but did not wire that operation into orderly ownership teardown. No symbol+mechanism+impact match exists in the current scratch index or issue history.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA, and the shutdown ordering, no-event manager stop, BACKUP-only clear, and authoritative Kea semantics are unchanged there.

### A7-b1-02

Title: A DHCP lease timer can start a non-cancellable full apply after shutdown's only apply drain

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:49-56` makes background applies wait forever and then run with a fresh non-cancellable context:

> 49 `func (d *Daemon) applyConfig(cfg *config.Config) {`
> 50 `    _ = d.applySem.Acquire(context.Background(), 1)`
> 51 `    defer d.applySem.Release(1)`
> 52 `    // Boot / DHCP-callback / feed / config-poll applies must always run to`
> 53 `    // completion (they are not request-bound and there is no operator waiting`
> 54 `    // to cancel them), so the heavy pipeline is driven with a non-cancellable`
> 55 `    // context -- byte-identical to the pre-#2926 behavior.`
> 56 `    if err := d.applyConfigLocked(context.Background(), cfg); err != nil {`

`pkg/daemon/daemon_run_shutdown.go:35-64` cancels and drains `applySem` once, then cancels the run context and waits its `WaitGroup`. DHCP clients are deliberately based on `context.Background()` and survive signal shutdown (`pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:275-280`); their independent `time.AfterFunc` invokes the callback at `:500-512`. `onDHCPAddressChange` can call the full `d.applyConfig(activeCfg)` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:73-114`, and neither the client nor timer belongs to the shutdown wait group.

Trace: A lease update arms the two-second recompile timer. Shutdown cancels the current apply and successfully acquires/releases `applySem`, establishing a false drain point. The timer then fires, reads the still-live active config, acquires `applySem` with `Background`, and starts the full networkd/netlink/FRR/IPsec/dataplane/HA apply. Concurrent shutdown proceeds to fence RGs and stop VRRP, cluster comms, FRR, and the dataplane. The late apply can re-arm state against stopped owners, access managers during teardown, or delay process exit with work shutdown can no longer cancel or join.

Refutation attempt: Canceling the signal/run context does not reach DHCP clients, by explicit design. `applyCancel` does not reach this apply because both semaphore acquisition and `applyConfigLocked` receive new Background contexts. The first semaphore drain covers callbacks already queued ahead of it, not a timer that enters afterward. Process exit eventually kills the goroutine, but only after the race with ordered teardown. GH #6716 is not a defense: it concerns a pre-lock active-config snapshot and still leaves this post-drain lifecycle entry possible.

HPC/invariant check: Cold lifecycle invariant violated: after the apply drain point, no producer may enter `applyConfigLocked`, and every producer that can do so must be quiesced and joined before dependent managers are torn down. Preserving DHCP addresses does not require preserving callback execution.

Why it matters: The shutdown fence is a failover safety boundary. Re-entering the full apply behind it can extend dual ownership, restore state on a demoting node, race external command execution, or dereference service owners after stop.

Fix direction: Give the DHCP manager a `QuiescePreservingLeases` operation that atomically disables/stops the recompile timer, suppresses new callbacks, cancels and joins client workers without deleting installed addresses, and call it before the final apply drain. Also gate every background apply on a daemon generation/context and reject entry after teardown begins. Add a deterministic timer-after-drain test asserting no apply or manager call occurs after the boundary.

Labels: MATERIAL, daemon-lifecycle, DHCP-client, apply-order, shutdown-race, goroutine, timer, netlink, userspace-live

Dedup note: Open GH #6716 matches `onDHCPAddressChange` reading `ActiveConfig` before `applySem`, with stale-snapshot overwrite impact. This finding matches a different mechanism: a Background-owned timer enters after the shutdown drain and races manager teardown. The ip-monitor Background semaphore shutdown issue in checked-in history is also a different producer/stop cycle. No current entry matches this timer+post-drain trace.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; the independent DHCP context/timer, callback, Background apply, and one-time shutdown drain are unchanged.

### A7-b1-03

Title: Bootstrap treats a failed lifeline netlink snapshot as DHCP and then cycles the management NIC

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:917-924` converts an empty address observation into an authoritative DHCP networkd file:

> 917 `// Snapshot the lifeline's addressing ONCE (Copilot: avoid the duplicate`
> 918 `// netlink walk). DHCP-managed or address-less lifelines get a plain DHCP`
> 919 `// .network; a statically-addressed one gets an Address=/Gateway= snapshot.`
> 920 `v4, v6, gw4, gw6 := interfaceAddrSnapshot(lifeline)`
> 921 `var content string`
> 922 `if isDHCPManaged(lifeline) || (len(v4) == 0 && len(v6) == 0) {`
> 923 `    content = "# Managed by xpfd -- #1922 bootstrap lifeline (DHCP)\n" +`
> 924 `        "[Match]\nName=fxp0\n\n[Network]\nDHCP=yes\n\n[DHCPv4]\nUseDNS=yes\nUseRoutes=yes\n"`

The observation function returns exactly that empty tuple on `LinkByName` failure and discards `AddrList` errors (`pkg/daemon/bootstrap.go:974-982`); it also continues past each `RouteList` error (`:993-997`). The caller writes the resulting `.network`, writes `.link`, renames/cycles to `fxp0`, and reloads networkd at `:886-905`.

Trace: A remote operator reaches a cold-boot appliance over a statically addressed enumeration-index-0 management NIC. Lifeline route discovery succeeds, but the later address or route netlink dump transiently fails. `interfaceAddrSnapshot` represents uncertainty as empty data. `writeBootstrapLifelineNetwork` chooses `DHCP=yes` (or omits the static default gateway), after which the caller renames and cycles the only reachable NIC. If the segment has no DHCP server, or if the lost gateway was required, the old static lifeline cannot return under `fxp0` and remote management is lost.

Refutation attempt: The earlier lifeline discovery does not preserve the address/prefix/gateway payload, only interface identity. `isDHCPManaged` is ORed with the empty snapshot condition, so a correctly detected static owner cannot prevent the fallback. Networkd reload cannot reconstruct data never written. The index-0 guard narrows the trigger but this is exactly the NIC the function is willing to cycle. The ignored writer/rename/reload errors were excluded from this finding because GH #5842 already owns that laundering mechanism.

HPC/invariant check: Bootstrap safety invariant violated: management-interface mutation may proceed only from a complete, successful lifeline snapshot. Unknown observation state must be distinct from a valid address-less/DHCP state; no hot-path cost is involved.

Why it matters: A transient netlink read failure during first boot can turn a healthy static management path into an unrecoverable remote lockout precisely while bootstrap is intended to preserve it.

Fix direction: Return a typed snapshot plus error, propagate address and route dump failures, and abort before writing `.network`/`.link` or cycling the link when the observation is incomplete. Distinguish an intentionally empty snapshot from read failure. Add injected LinkByName/AddrList/RouteList failure tests that assert zero file, rename, link-cycle, and reload calls.

Labels: MATERIAL, bootstrap, management-lifeline, netlink, systemd-networkd, cold-boot, remote-lockout, userspace-live

Dedup note: Open GH #5842 matches `writeLinkFile`/rename/networkd reload error laundering and management lockout. A7-b1-03 is rooted earlier at `interfaceAddrSnapshot`: failed observation is positively misclassified as DHCP or a gateway-free static snapshot, even if all later writes and commands succeed. No current index/history entry names that symbol+mechanism+impact combination.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; snapshot error swallowing, DHCP classification, and rename/reload ordering are unchanged.

### A7-b1-04

Title: Normal apply discards every login, sudoers, deprovision, sshd, and root-auth failure

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:97-104` explicitly limits error collection to shutdown closeout:

> 97 `// Steps 11-13 are the login/credential reconcilers. They return their`
> 98 `// accumulated failures (#5874) so the cancel closeout can surface them,`
> 99 `// but on the NORMAL apply path the returns are intentionally DISCARDED:`
> 100 `// the tail is best-effort here because the next boot re-renders login /`
> 101 `// sudoers / SSH / root-auth from the active config, so a transient failure`
> 102 `// converges (the #2926 next-boot contract). Only the daemon-stop cancel`
> 103 `// closeout -- where next-boot convergence does NOT happen while the daemon`
> 104 `// stays intentionally stopped -- collects and fails on these.`

The five calls are assigned to `_` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:106-127`. The final `errors.Join` at `:316-327` includes networkd, dataplane, Kea, nft, IPsec, interface, route-leak, rule, management-route, VRF, and VRRP failures, but none of those credential-owner errors. The closeout owner list at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_hostauth.go:47-62` confirms that each function already returns an actionable error and is considered part of host authorization.

Trace: An operator removes a user, downgrades a class, rotates root authentication, or disables root SSH. The corresponding filesystem ownership, `useradd`/`chpasswd`, sudoers write, authorized-keys revoke, sshd config write, or service reload fails. The function returns an error, but normal apply discards it and the commit reports success. The stale password/key, NOPASSWD grant, or `PermitRootLogin` state remains effective with no retry debt; only an unrelated later apply or reboot may try again.

Refutation attempt: "Next boot" is neither a bounded runtime retry nor acceptable confirmation for a security-revocation commit. The owners run independently, so collecting errors does not require short-circuiting later steps. Existing owner tests prove local failure returns and the shutdown-closeout tests prove aggregation is feasible, but no normal-tail test requires propagation. Closed owner-specific issues fixed reconcile semantics, not this call-site discard.

HPC/invariant check: Security apply invariant violated: a successful commit may be reported only after every owner of host-login authorization either converges or records a surfaced failure/debt. These are cold apply operations; joining their existing errors adds no hot-path cost.

Why it matters: Operators can receive a successful commit while credentials they explicitly revoked remain usable indefinitely. That is a durable privilege-retention failure, not merely delayed cosmetic state.

Fix direction: Run all five owners, collect every returned error, and include them in the tail's final `errors.Join`; keep collect-all ordering so one failure does not suppress later revocations. Record health/retry debt for background applies that have no commit caller. Add injected-failure tests for each owner proving normal commit fails while all later owners still execute.

Labels: MATERIAL, host-integration, authentication, authorization, sudoers, sshd, systemd, apply-error, privilege-retention, userspace-live

Dedup note: Closed #3889, #5128, and related issues repaired individual sudo/user cleanup semantics. #5874 wires these errors into shutdown's host-auth closeout. A7-b1-04 is the distinct normal-path call-site mechanism at `applyTailReconciles`, where all five results are intentionally discarded and absent from the final join. No exact current issue matches it.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; the five discarded returns and final error set are unchanged.

### A7-b1-05

Title: Fabric IPVLAN apply converts terminal netlink failures into success and has no persistent recovery owner

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_interfaces.go:86-95` logs exhaustion and then returns no error to the apply transaction:

> 86 `retryErr = ensureFabricIPVLAN(parentLinux, fabLinux, addrs)`
> 87 `if retryErr == nil {`
> 88 `    break`
> 89 `}`
> 90 `}`
> 91 `if retryErr != nil {`
> 92 `    slog.Error("CRITICAL: fabric IPVLAN creation failed after retries -- cluster heartbeat will not work",`
> 93 `        "parent", parentLinux, "name", fabLinux, "err", retryErr)`
> 94 `}`
> 95 `continue`

`applyFabricIPVLAN` is void and its caller cannot add the failure to apply debt. `ensureFabricIPVLAN` also logs and ignores parent-up/MTU, overlay MTU, and configured `AddrReplace` failures before returning nil (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_fabric.go:29-50,72-96`). Fabric session/config sync waits only 30 times for an address and then exits (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:793-812`); heartbeat startup likewise has a terminal 30x2s budget at `:1304-1348`. None of those consumers recreates the overlay.

Trace: On cold boot, parent readiness, device creation, namespace state, or address installation remains unavailable past the fixed apply retry window. A `LinkAdd` failure is logged after six attempts and forgotten; an `AddrReplace` failure is even reported as a successful ensure. The config apply completes successfully. Session/config sync and, where configured on that path, heartbeat resolve no local address, exhaust their independent minute-long waits, and exit permanently. No level-triggered owner retries the desired overlay; only an unrelated config apply or daemon restart can heal it.

Refutation attempt: Networkd can configure an address only after the expected netdev exists and is matched; it cannot recover a permanently absent overlay on behalf of this imperative owner. Consumer retries observe addresses but never call `ensureFabricIPVLAN`. The userspace XSK callback supplies at most another untracked attempt and itself only logs failure. Closed #127 repaired address reconciliation when an existing overlay is observed; it did not propagate failures or establish retry debt. The failure can isolate HA control traffic, so it remains High despite requiring a prolonged/transient cold-boot fault.

HPC/invariant check: Control-plane convergence invariant violated: every configured fabric overlay and address must have one level-triggered owner that retries until success or daemon cancellation, and apply success must mean the required netlink state was observed. Work is cold-path and may be event/timer driven without touching packet processing.

Why it matters: A recoverable boot-order race can become permanent cluster isolation for the lifetime of xpfd. Config/session sync disappears, heartbeat may disappear, and ownership safety can degrade or split while the active configuration is reported as applied.

Fix direction: Make `ensureFabricIPVLAN` return all link/MTU/address/up failures and make `applyFabricIPVLAN` return an aggregate error into the apply tail. Add a daemon-context, generation-fenced reconciliation loop driven by link events plus bounded backoff that continues until the overlay and addresses are observed. Consumers should depend on readiness rather than carry their own terminal retry budgets. Test transient LinkAdd and AddrReplace failures followed by recovery without another commit.

Labels: MATERIAL, HA, fabric, IPVLAN, netlink, cold-boot, retry-debt, session-sync, heartbeat, userspace-live

Dedup note: `claude-review-002` matches `applyFabricIPVLAN` sleeping five seconds while holding `applySem`, with commit/config-sync latency impact. `gemini-review-042` matches the disabled `continue` and loss of AF_XDP zero-copy. Closed #127 matches omission of address reconciliation on an already-existing overlay. A7-b1-05 instead matches swallowed terminal netlink outcomes plus the absence of a persistent owner, causing reported convergence and long-lived HA isolation.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; void apply, ignored netlink errors, finite retries, and consumer exit paths are unchanged.

### A7-b1-06

Title: DNS ownership failures are warning-only, so a successful commit can leave stale or dual resolvers

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_dns.go:197-205` discards the systemd-resolved ownership failure:

> 197 `func (r *dnsReconciler) reconcile(in system.ResolvedDropinInput, bootEmptyRepairOnly bool) {`
> 198 `    // Always converge resolved off + remove stale drop-ins, regardless of`
> 199 `    // whether resolv.conf needs rewriting, so a previously-installed`
> 200 `    // drop-in / running resolved is cleaned up even on an idempotent pass.`
> 201 `    if err := r.disableMaskResolved(); err != nil {`
> 202 `        // Do NOT proceed assuming resolved is off -- it would be a second`
> 203 `        // owner. Still own resolv.conf (a static file wins over an`
> 204 `        // inactive stub), but surface the failure loudly.`
> 205 `        slog.Warn("DNS: failed to disable+mask systemd-resolved; it may remain a second resolver owner", "err", err)`

Stale drop-in removals are also warning-only at `pkg/daemon/daemon_dns.go:207-210`, and an atomic `/etc/resolv.conf` write failure logs and returns from the void method at `:238-240`. `reconcileDNSLocked` is void (`:351-357`), and `applyTailReconciles` invokes it without an error slot at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:58-70`.

Trace: A runtime commit removes or changes static name servers while `systemctl`, drop-in removal, or the atomic resolv.conf replacement fails. The old file, symlink target, drop-in, or resolved service remains authoritative. The DNS reconciler returns no result, the apply tail reports success, and no retry debt is retained. With no subsequent DHCP event or commit, the appliance resolves through stale servers or has two competing owners indefinitely.

Refutation attempt: Writing a regular resolv.conf can dominate a running resolved stub in some layouts, but the same function acknowledges the second-owner state and write failure can leave the old target untouched. Logging is not convergence and there is no periodic DNS owner. The boot repair guard protects a good preexisting file only for the intentional empty-merge case; it does not convert I/O/service failures into success. Closed #1715 fixed the ownership architecture, not error propagation from its replacement reconciler.

HPC/invariant check: Host-integration invariant violated: exactly one resolver owner and the requested resolver content must be observed before apply success. DNS reconciliation is cold-path systemd/filesystem work; returning an error has no forwarding cost.

Why it matters: Control-plane package updates, NTP, remote logging, DDNS, and operator commands can continue using removed servers or lose name resolution while the configuration transaction reports green.

Fix direction: Return and aggregate disable/mask, stale-drop-in, inspection, and write failures from `dnsReconciler.reconcile` through `reconcileDNSLocked` into the apply tail. Preserve collect-all behavior and establish bounded background retry/health debt for DHCP-triggered paths. Add failure-injection tests for systemctl, remove, Lstat/read, and atomic write.

Labels: MATERIAL, DNS, systemd-resolved, resolv-conf, filesystem, apply-error, retry-debt, host-integration, userspace-live

Dedup note: Closed #1715 covers the prior conflicting owners and dangling symlink architecture. This finding is a residual in the replacement symbols `dnsReconciler.reconcile`/`reconcileDNSLocked`: all ownership and write errors are converted to warnings, giving successful commit plus stale/dual state. No exact current symbol+mechanism+impact entry exists.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; the void reconciler chain and warning-only failures are unchanged.

### A7-b1-07

Title: Standalone router advertisements have no retry owner after an asynchronous sender bind failure

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_routing.go:39-47` performs a one-shot standalone apply and treats even synchronous failure as warning-only:

> 39 `if !isCluster {`
> 40 `    if d.ra != nil && len(raConfigs) > 0 {`
> 41 `        if err := d.ra.Apply(raConfigs); err != nil {`
> 42 `            slog.Warn("failed to apply RA config", "err", err)`
> 43 `        }`
> 44 `    } else if d.ra != nil {`
> 45 `        // No RA configs remain -- the operator removed all RA. Gracefully`
> 46 `        // WITHDRAW any previous senders (final lifetime-0 goodbye, #5092)`
> 47 `        // instead of a hard Clear, so hosts drop this router immediately`

The RA sender opens its NDP socket asynchronously and `start()` always returns nil (`pkg/ra/sender.go:203-211`). If the bounded open fails, the owner exits and remains detectable as dead; `pkg/ra/ra.go:429-449` rebuilds it only on the next `Apply`. Cluster mode has a digest that advances only after success plus periodic/event-driven reconciliation (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ra_reconcile.go:39-81`), while that method returns immediately for standalone at `:50-53`.

Trace: On standalone cold boot, a configured interface is still settling, lacks its link-local address, or cannot bind the NDP socket during the sender's roughly two-second retry. The asynchronous goroutine dies after `d.ra.Apply` has already returned success. No standalone RA reconcile ticker or link-event owner calls the same desired state again. Hosts receive no periodic or solicited RA until an unrelated commit/DHCP reapply/restart happens to invoke `Apply`.

Refutation attempt: #2865 correctly makes a subsequent `Apply` recognize and rebuild a dead sender, but standalone mode does not guarantee a subsequent apply. The sender's internal bounded retry reduces probability but does not create convergence after the bound. Cluster's safety pass cannot help because it explicitly rejects standalone config. Synchronous `Apply` errors are also only logged, reinforcing the missing debt. This is Medium because IPv6 hosts may have static/default alternatives and the trigger requires startup timing or socket failure.

HPC/invariant check: Service convergence invariant violated: configured RA service must be level-triggered until every sender is live, and a dead async owner must retain retry debt. Detection/retry belongs to cold control-plane events or a low-rate timer, not the packet hot path.

Why it matters: A transient boot-order or capability failure can become a full-lifetime IPv6 default-router outage on a standalone appliance while configuration and daemon health appear normal.

Fix direction: Extend the digest/reconcile owner to standalone mode, or add link-event plus periodic reconciliation that validates sender liveness and retries unchanged desired state. Advance any desired hash only after all senders report a live socket; surface immediate failures into apply health. Add a deterministic failed-first-open test that recovers without a config change.

Labels: MATERIAL, router-advertisement, IPv6, standalone, cold-boot, async-start, retry-debt, host-networking, userspace-live

Dedup note: Closed #2865 matches `ra.Manager.Apply` retaining a dead sender as unchanged; it added dead detection on the next apply. A7-b1-07 is the daemon-side residual at `applyServicesReconcile`/`reconcileClusterRAServices`: standalone has no guaranteed next apply, so the repaired manager is never re-entered. No current entry matches that symbol+mechanism+outage combination.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; one-shot standalone apply, async nil return, dead-sender rebuild-on-next-apply, and cluster-only retry are unchanged.

### A7-b1-08

Title: LLDP caches desired state before a partial void apply, suppressing recovery on unchanged config

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:410-418` records the desired generation before calling the manager:

> 410 `// Skip when the effective config is unchanged since the last reconcile, so`
> 411 `// an unrelated commit never bounces a healthy LLDP generation (sockets +`
> 412 `// neighbor table). The first reconcile (boot) always runs.`
> 413 `if d.lldpApplyInit && lldpConfigEqual(d.lldpApplied, want) {`
> 414 `    return`
> 415 `}`
> 416 `d.lldpApplyInit = true`
> 417 `d.lldpApplied = want`
> 418 ``

The subsequent `d.lldpMgr.Apply(ctx, want)` has no result (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply_tail.go:426-430`). The manager first stops the complete prior generation, then logs and skips each missing interface or raw-socket setup failure while continuing (`pkg/lldp/lldp.go:263-317`).

Trace: A commit or cold boot requests LLDP on several interfaces. A rename/link race, missing capability, or AF_PACKET bind failure affects one interface. `Manager.Apply` has already stopped the old generation, silently omits the failed interface, and returns void. The daemon cache nevertheless says the complete desired state was applied. Any later commit carrying the same effective LLDP config returns at the equality guard, and there is no link-event or periodic owner to retry the omitted session.

Refutation attempt: Healthy sessions continue after creation, but there is no recovery path for a session that was never created. The idempotence guard is correct only if apply is all-or-observable-partial. Existing tests verify skip identity and lifecycle serialization, not injected interface/socket failure followed by unchanged desired state. A daemon restart heals only by reconstructing the owner, which is not runtime convergence.

HPC/invariant check: Reconcile-cache invariant violated: `applied == desired` may be published only after every desired LLDP interface has a live session, or the cache must encode partial outcomes and retry debt. This is low-rate control-plane work and does not require packet-hot-path changes.

Why it matters: LLDP can disappear indefinitely from one or all ports after a transient host-integration failure, hiding topology and neighbor identity while commits report success and future identical reconciles are suppressed.

Fix direction: Make `lldp.Manager.Apply` return per-interface/aggregate outcomes, cache only proven-live desired state, and retain failed-interface debt for link-event/timer retry. Prefer building new sessions before stopping healthy unchanged sessions. Add tests for missing interface and socket-open failure, then recovery with byte-identical config.

Labels: MATERIAL, LLDP, AF_PACKET, lifecycle, reconcile-cache, retry-debt, interface-race, observability, userspace-live

Dedup note: Existing LLDP history covers identifier collisions, TTL bounds, and manager stop/apply lifecycle. None matches `Daemon.reconcileLLDP` advancing `lldpApplied` before a void partial apply and thereby suppressing unchanged-state retry. No exact symbol+mechanism+impact entry was found.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; cache-before-apply and manager log-and-skip semantics are unchanged.

### A7-b1-09

Title: The netlink lo0 renderer panics on nil filter or term slots tolerated by sibling config walkers

Severity: Medium

Confidence: Medium

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:174-182` treats map-key presence as a non-nil filter/term guarantee:

> 174 `func toNftLo0Spec(cfg *config.Config, filterV4, filterV6 string) xnft.Lo0FilterSpec {`
> 175 `    var spec xnft.Lo0FilterSpec`
> 176 `    pl := cfg.PolicyOptions.PrefixLists`
> 177 `    if filterV4 != "" {`
> 178 `        if f, ok := cfg.Firewall.FiltersInet[filterV4]; ok {`
> 179 `            for _, term := range f.Terms {`
> 180 `                spec.V4Terms = append(spec.V4Terms, toNftLo0Term(term, pl))`
> 181 `            }`
> 182 `        }`

`toNftLo0Term` immediately dereferences `term` at `pkg/daemon/daemon_nft_netlink.go:194-207`. The strict reference validator likewise checks only map-key existence (`pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go:320-332`) and explicitly supports tolerant paths. In contrast, the userspace snapshot walker treats nil filters and nil/all-nil terms as a supported empty collection (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/filters.go:79-93`), pinned by `protocol_null_collections_2214_test.go:104-123`.

Trace: A tolerant/programmatic config shape contains the referenced firewall map key with a nil filter value, or a filter whose term slice contains a nil slot. The strict reference check sees the key as defined. During normal apply, `applyLo0Filter` calls `toNftLo0Spec` before installer error handling or cold-boot fencing. The nil dereference panics xpfd; the same persisted shape can repeat on restart before host-bound policy convergence.

Refutation attempt: Normal strict text compilation constructs non-nil filter and term values, so this is not an ordinary CLI reproducer and Confidence is Medium. However, sibling production code and tests explicitly establish nil typed-collection shapes as a tolerated/programmatic invariant, and the strict validator's key-only check does not exclude them. `applyLo0Filter` has no recover boundary, so installer fail-closed logic never runs. The finding is Medium rather than High because the trigger requires malformed internal/tolerant state.

HPC/invariant check: Tolerant-config invariant violated: every pointer collection walker must either skip nil values consistently or return a typed fail-closed error before dereference. This renderer is cold-path; nil guards are negligible.

Why it matters: A recoverable malformed slot becomes a daemon crash/restart loop at the primary kernel host-filter renderer instead of preserving the prior nft generation or installing the existing cold-boot fence.

Fix direction: Make the reference validator require a non-nil value, make `toNftLo0Spec` return `(spec, error)`, and reject/skip nil terms consistently with a fail-closed result. Ensure `applyLo0Filter` reaches fence/error handling rather than panicking. Add nil-filter and nil-term tests through the real apply conversion path.

Labels: MATERIAL, nftables, netlink, lo0, nil-safety, tolerant-config, cold-boot, host-protection, userspace-live

Dedup note: #2214 hardens the userspace JSON snapshot against nil filter/term collections, and #3296 validates dangling filter names. A7-b1-09 is the sibling kernel renderer at `toNftLo0Spec`/`toNftLo0Term`, where a present-but-nil value passes name validation and panics before nft fail-closed handling. No current exact match was found.

Verified against origin/master: Yes. Fresh `origin/master` is the setup SHA; key-only validation, unguarded renderer dereferences, and sibling nil tolerance are unchanged.

- Dedup inputs: the complete 722-line scratch index (290 fresh open GitHub issues, 354 prior-review entries, 77 prior-final entries) plus symbol/mechanism/impact searches in `docs/issues/issue-history.md`.

## Triage result

Outcome: **10 `MATERIAL` issues** suitable for individual filing and **1 `COHORT` issue containing 2 low-materiality survivors**. Ten already-tracked issue surfaces were suppressed as duplicates. No candidate was retired as `STALE`, and no source file was edited.

| Finding | Area | Gate verdict | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | FRR routes | MATERIAL | Unvalidated or leniently retained route operands are emitted verbatim and can reject the whole managed reload. |
| F2 | FRR BGP/BFD | MATERIAL | Neighbor identity is not constrained to one FRR token and is reused raw at all neighbor/BFD sites. |
| F3 | Host credentials | MATERIAL | Marker-first ownership can overclaim an existing credential when the following mutation fails. |
| F4 | Host credentials | MATERIAL | Inventory and marker read errors collapse to absence, allowing false-success revocation closeout. |
| F5 | networkd/netlink | MATERIAL | Teardown destroys its durable evidence on transient lookup, file-removal, and reload failures. |
| F6 | HA/RG state | MATERIAL | The periodic reconciler can commit an epoch-stale RG state and temporarily erase retry debt. |
| F7 | system services | MATERIAL | chrony, rsyslog, and sshd filesystem convergence erases failed runtime reload debt. |
| F8 | NIC tunables | MATERIAL | Removing an interface from the userspace allowlist leaves RSS/coalescence changes behind. |
| F9 | host-inbound | MATERIAL | A failed conntrack flush retains old authorization without an autonomous retry. |
| F10 | management API | MATERIAL | An unexpectedly dead listener is diagnosed but not restarted when the desired endpoint is unchanged. |
| C1 | Host convergence/latency | COHORT | Hostname durability retry and aggregate sequential ethtool latency are real but low-materiality. |

## High-confidence material findings

### F1

Title: FRR non-protocol route rendering lacks a final operand-validity belt

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:165-169` accepts a generate-route destination without a key validator:

```go
165 "generate": {desc: "Generated routes", children: map[string]*schemaNode{
166     "route": {desc: "Generated route", args: 1, placeholder: "<destination>", children: map[string]*schemaNode{
167         "policy":  {desc: "Policy", args: 1, placeholder: "<policy>", children: nil},
168         "discard": {desc: "Discard route", children: nil},
169     }},
```

`pkg/frr/config_render.go:245-254` classifies the raw string by colon and emits it directly:

```go
245 func renderGenerateRoutes(b *strings.Builder, fc *FullConfig) {
246     if len(fc.GenerateRoutes) == 0 {
247         return
248     }
249     for _, gr := range fc.GenerateRoutes {
250         if strings.Contains(gr.Prefix, ":") {
251             fmt.Fprintf(b, "ipv6 route %s blackhole\n", gr.Prefix)
252         } else {
253             fmt.Fprintf(b, "ip route %s blackhole\n", gr.Prefix)
254         }
```

The backup-router validator explicitly downgrades malformed input on tolerant load, promising omission at `pkg/config/compiler_system.go:2531-2539`:

```go
2531 if net.ParseIP(nh) == nil {
2532     msg := fmt.Sprintf(
2533         "system backup-router %s: not a valid IP address; FRR rejects a "+
2534             "malformed next-hop, which fails the entire static config "+
2535             "load (frr-reload)", nh)
2536     if !lenient {
2537         return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", msg)
2538     }
2539     warnings = append(warnings, msg+" (ignored: backup-router default route not installed until corrected)")
```

The renderer does not implement that promise at `pkg/frr/config_render.go:365-370`:

```go
365 prefix := "ip"
366 if nhV6 || strings.Contains(dst, ":") {
367     prefix = "ipv6"
368 }
369 fmt.Fprintf(b, "%s route %s %s 250\n", prefix, dst, fc.BackupRouter)
370 b.WriteString("!\n")
```

The same mechanism affects leniently retained static routes: `generateStaticRouteInTable` uses `sr.Destination`, `nh.Address`, and `nh.Interface` directly at `pkg/frr/config_render.go:123-236`; `compiler_validate_warn.go:646-657` warns about malformed static destinations but does not remove them.

Trace: (1) An operator can commit `routing-options generate route "not a prefix"` because the schema declares one argument but no destination validator. Alternatively, an older persisted or HA-synced malformed static/backup route is retained by the tolerant compiler. (2) `assembleFRRConfig` copies those typed values into `FullConfig`. (3) `renderGenerateRoutes`, `generateStaticRouteInTable`, or `renderBackupRouter` writes the raw operand into the managed section. (4) `frr-reload.py` feeds the section to vtysh as one reload; an invalid static command returns non-zero. (5) The new managed FRR configuration does not converge, affecting valid routes and protocols that shared the reload.

Refutation attempt: I checked the static-route key validators, strict backup-router checks, tolerant warning pass, full-config assembler, global control-character walk, and FRR render validators. Strict static/backup commits are protected, but those errors are intentionally warnings on boot/HA sync; generate-route has no strict destination validator at all. Control-character sanitization prevents multiline injection, not malformed CIDR/IP/interface operands. No renderer-side predicate omits these route objects, and assigned tests cover valid generate/backup/static output only.

HPC/invariant check: This is outside the packet hot path. The violated convergence invariant is that tolerant boot/HA input may warn and omit an unsafe object but must not poison the shared FRR reload or publish runtime convergence before success.

Why it matters: One malformed generated or leniently retained route can prevent all valid FRR changes from loading at cold boot or after HA sync, leaving routing unavailable or stale rather than isolating the bad route as the warning promises.

Fix direction: Add `ValidateRouteDestination` (or a generate-specific CIDR validator) to the generate-route identity. Add shared render-side validators for static destination/next-hop/interface and backup destination/next-hop; on tolerant input, log and omit only the invalid route. Add strict generate rejection plus lenient-load/HA-sync tests that assert valid sibling routes still reload.

Labels: bug, frr, routing, cold-boot, ha-sync, convergence, vsrx-parity

Dedup note: Distinct from closed #2891/#2911/#4808, which added backup family/strict validation but not tolerant render omission, and from closed #4097, which covered multiline community/as-path values. Symbol, mechanism, and whole-reload impact searches found no current open issue for non-protocol route operand omission.

Verified against origin/master: `git show origin/master:pkg/frr/config_render.go` still has raw generate emission at lines 245-254, raw static operands at 123-236, and unconditional backup emission at 365-370; `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:165-169` still lacks the validator. Title: BGP neighbor identity can span multiple FRR tokens and is reused raw by BGP and BFD

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: The neighbor identity has no key validator at `pkg/config/schema_routing.go:402-407`:


The same raw identity reaches global BFD at `pkg/frr/bfd.go:85-93`:

```go

87     // `router ... vrf` and static-route vrf clauses. A leniently-loaded
88     // control character in the instance name would otherwise inject a
89     // standalone line into the managed `bfd` block.
90     fmt.Fprintf(&b, " peer %s vrf %s\n", p.address, sanitizeFRRValue(p.vrfName))
91 } else {
92     fmt.Fprintf(&b, " peer %s\n", p.address)

```

Every BGP neighbor directive likewise formats `n.Address` raw, beginning at `pkg/frr/protocols_render.go:291-317`.

Trace: (1) A quoted neighbor identity containing ordinary ASCII whitespace passes schema validation and the global C0/DEL guard. (2) Compilation retains the complete string with a non-zero peer AS. (3) `validNeighbors` admits it. (4) BGP declaration, activation, route-map, password/BFD directives, and the global BFD peer split the identity into multiple FRR lexer tokens. (5) The resulting commands are rejected or interpreted with different line-local grammar, causing the shared managed reload to fail for otherwise valid peers.

Refutation attempt: I checked schema key validators, compiler BGP gates, `validNeighbors`, `sanitizeFRRValue`, `frrTokenUnsafeIndex`, the #4588 status-query IP guard, and all neighbor/BFD interpolation sites. The global guard rejects C0/DEL and therefore blocks newline command injection, but deliberately preserves space. `frrTokenUnsafeIndex` is used for whitespace-split authentication values, not neighbor identities. #4588 protects read commands only. Peer-AS validation does not constrain the address token.

HPC/invariant check: No packet-path or cache-line concern applies. The violated parser-boundary invariant is that a value occupying one FRR token must be validated as exactly one token before every interpolation site shares it.

Why it matters: A single malformed neighbor can reject a whole FRR reload, taking unrelated BGP peers and routing changes out of convergence; BFD configuration is poisoned by the same identity.

Fix direction: Define one neighbor-identity validator shared by schema/compiler and renderer. Accept the intended set (bare IP, and only explicitly supported hostname/interface/peer-group forms) while rejecting whitespace and FRR token metacharacters. ### F3

Title: Marker-first credential ownership can overclaim pre-existing credentials after a failed mutation

Severity: High

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: Key ownership is durably claimed before any directory/chown/content mutation at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1176-1185`:

```go
1176 // #5841 marker-first: record SSH-KEY ownership BEFORE writing
1177 // authorized_keys. This is a DISTINCT marker from the
1178 // password/account markers, so setting only a password never claims
1179 // the key file — the emptied-key / deprovision reconcilers only
1180 // remove a key file this marker proves xpf wrote. Written
1181 // unconditionally (idempotent) so an upgrade that already has
1182 // xpf-written keys but no key marker gains one on the next apply.
1183 // Fail VISIBLE: if the durable marker cannot be written, skip the
1184 // key write and retry next apply rather than leave a
1185 // written-but-unmarked key grant (the underclaim).
```

The following durable write can fail without rolling that newly created marker back at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1231-1236`:

```go
1231 if err := fsatomic.WriteFileDurable(keysFile, []byte(keysContent), 0600, fsatomic.WithOwner(uid, gid)); err != nil {
1232     slog.Warn("failed to write authorized_keys",
1233         "user", user.Name, "err", err)
1234     fail(fmt.Errorf("write authorized_keys for %s: %w", user.Name, err))
1235     continue
1236 }
```

Password and root-key paths have the same ordering at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1457-1487` and `1823-1863`. Later removal trusts `passwordProvisioned`/`keyProvisioned` and locks or removes the resource (`1240-1270`, `1494-1507`, and `login_password.go:507-556`).

Trace: (1) A pre-existing account has an operator-managed password or `authorized_keys`. (2) Config asks xpf to replace that resource. (3) xpf writes a durable ownership marker. (4) `chpasswd`, mkdir/chown, or `WriteFileDurable` fails, or power is lost in that interval, so the pre-existing credential remains unchanged. (5) Before a successful retry, config removes the credential/user. (6) Revoke sees the marker as proof xpf created the still-pre-existing resource and locks the password or deletes the key file.

Refutation attempt: I checked resource-specific UID markers, marker-write failure tests, retry behavior, deprovision scoping, root parity, and crash durability. Resource-specific markers solve cross-resource and UID-reuse errors, and marker-first prevents the older underclaim. They do not distinguish a newly recorded intent from a successfully mutated resource. No failure branch removes only a newly created marker; no pending/committed phase exists. The assigned #5841 test injects marker-write failure, not mutation failure after marker success.

HPC/invariant check: This is durable ownership state, not a hot path. The violated crash invariant is two-phase ownership: destructive cleanup may rely only on a committed marker proving the mutation completed, while retry intent must survive separately.

Why it matters: A transient command/filesystem failure or power cut can turn an operator-owned login credential into an xpf-owned one and later delete or lock it, causing administrative lockout and crossing the intended ownership boundary.

Fix direction: Introduce crash-recoverable pending and committed ownership states. Record pending intent before mutation; promote to committed only after success. On failure, remove a newly created pending marker while preserving any pre-existing committed marker. Revocation must trust committed state only. Add password, user-key, and root-key tests for mutation failure, crash-state recovery, config removal before retry, and already-owned retries.

Labels: bug, security, host-auth, lifecycle, durability, cold-boot

Dedup note: This is the inverse residual of closed #5841: that issue fixed mutated-but-unmarked underclaim and cross-resource ownership. The current mechanism is marked-but-not-mutated overclaim with destructive cleanup. No current open issue or prior review entry matched this symbol/mechanism/impact tuple.

Verified against origin/master: Marker-before-mutation ordering and absence of rollback remain at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:1176-1236,1457-1487,1823-1863`; marker-based destructive branches remain in `daemon_system.go` and `login_password.go:507-556` on tip `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

(5) The stale transition removes blackholes. (6) The node can forward as active until the next two-second sweep recomputes `active != applied` and repairs both effects.

Refutation attempt: I read all state-machine locking/epoch methods, event-handler completion logic, periodic-loop serialization, shutdown join, blackhole ordering, and current open HA issues. The mutex prevents data races but not stale external effects. Event handlers correctly use `ApplyIfCurrent`; the periodic path does not. A subsequent sweep self-heals, but no immediate trigger is wired and a two-second stale-active interval is enough to violate single-owner forwarding. GH#6530 is a separate peer-fence write with persistent blind debt.

HPC/invariant check: Atomic/cache-line concerns do not apply; calls are control-plane RPCs. The violated concurrency invariant is generation monotonicity: an external effect may be acknowledged and followed by dependent blackhole changes only if its captured epoch is still current; any stale completion must reassert debt immediately.

Why it matters: During failover, the old node can re-enter active forwarding and remove its blackholes after a newer demotion, creating a transient dual-active window, duplicate delivery/asymmetric state, and session divergence.

Fix direction: Route periodic completion through `ApplyIfCurrent(tr)` and skip dependent blackhole/readiness effects when stale. Better, re-read `(desired, epoch)` before the external call and retry a changed epoch in the same pass. Make `MarkApplied` set `applyPending = (applied != active)` defensively. Add a deterministic blocked-RPC interleaving test proving a newer demotion cannot be overwritten and no stale blackhole removal occurs.

Labels: bug, ha, race, vrrp, userspace-dataplane, failover

Dedup note: Closed #66 fixed stale cluster/VRRP event handlers; this is the residual periodic writer that still bypasses the epoch API. GH#6530 concerns peer-fence state not being recorded and a persistent blackhole, not a stale periodic completion. No current duplicate matched this interleaving.

Verified against origin/master: `git show` confirms `pkg/daemon/rg_state.go:163-171` still has non-epoch `MarkApplied`, and `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:807-848,854-861` still calls it and reconciles blackholes from `tr` on `origin/master` SHA `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

### F7

Title: Managed service file convergence erases failed runtime reload debt

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: chrony uses one context across source reload and all threshold fallbacks, logs failures, and returns no acknowledgement (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:508-517`):

```go
508 func reloadChronyRuntime(sourcesChanged, thresholdChanged bool) {
509     ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
510     defer cancel()
511
512     if sourcesChanged {
513         chronyCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "chronyc", "reload", "sources")
514         chronyCmd.WaitDelay = 5 * time.Second // post-SIGKILL pipe-drain cap (#1794)
515         if out, err := chronyCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
516             slog.Warn("failed to reload chrony sources", "err", err, "output", string(out))
517         }
```

The next unchanged apply skips runtime work at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:572-576`:

```go
572 if !sourcesChanged && !thresholdChanged {
573     return
574 }
575
576 reloadChronyRuntime(sourcesChanged, thresholdChanged)
```

rsyslog likewise keys restart solely to the just-observed disk delta at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:993-1002`:

```go
993 // Reconcile the on-disk managed drop-ins against `desired`. A removal OR a
994 // (re)write flips `changed`, which gates the single restart below.
995 changed := reconcileSyslogDropins(confDir, prefix, desired)
996
997 if changed {
998     if out, err := runCommandTimeout("systemctl", "restart", "rsyslog"); err != nil {
999         slog.Error("failed to restart rsyslog",
1000             "err", err, "output", strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
1001     } else {
1002         slog.Info("rsyslog file configs applied", "files", len(desired))
```

The sshd removal branch deletes the drop-in before reload and returns the failure (`daemon_system.go:1582-1600`), but a retry sees `!hadDropIn` and returns at lines 1585-1586. Update/rewrite reload failures restore prior content; removal failures do not have equivalent durable evidence.

Trace: (1) Config changes or removes chrony, rsyslog, or sshd managed files. (2) Atomic filesystem reconcile succeeds. (3) the runtime reload/restart fails or times out. (4) Current apply logs/returns a failure depending on service, but disk now equals desired. (5) The next apply computes `changed=false` or `hadDropIn=false` and skips the runtime command. (6) The daemon continues with old in-memory service behavior until an unrelated future file delta or process restart.

Refutation attempt: I checked command timeouts, per-service return values, caller aggregation, ssh update rollback, removal idempotency, and existing tests/issues. #1794 bounded individual commands and made errors visible; it did not retain a failed runtime generation. #2062 restores prior ssh content on update failure, but the remove path has nothing left to distinguish “removed and reloaded” from “removed but still live.” #5111 correctly marks successful syslog removal as a disk change, but that bit is ephemeral.

HPC/invariant check: These commands run under serialized apply, so no packet hot-path issue exists. The control-plane invariant is two-phase convergence: desired file generation and runtime-loaded generation need separate acknowledgement, and the latter must remain dirty after failure. chrony's shared context also lets one 15-second attempt exhaust every fallback, increasing apply latency without improving convergence.

Why it matters: Removed SSH policy can stay live, stale rsyslog forwarding can continue leaking or losing logs, and stale NTP source/threshold behavior can persist while subsequent applies appear quiescent.

Fix direction: Track a per-service desired generation and runtime-ack generation (durably where reboot behavior requires it), or preserve/recreate a reload-needed marker until command success. Return/aggregate chrony and rsyslog failures without discarding the debt. Give each chrony fallback its own bounded context or enforce one explicit aggregate deadline while still attempting viable fallbacks. Add fail-then-unchanged-retry tests for update and removal.

Labels: bug, systemd, chrony, rsyslog, sshd, retry-debt, convergence

Dedup note: Distinct residual from closed #1794 (unbounded command/error visibility), #2062 (sshd file lifecycle/update rollback), and #5111 (syslog removal change accounting). None tracks runtime acknowledgement across an unchanged next apply.

Verified against origin/master: `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:508-576,993-1004,1582-1600` retains the disk-delta-only gating on `origin/master` at `ad959117748181dabe46b8ddc2827de670380cea`.

### F8

Title: Shrinking the userspace interface allowlist leaves RSS and coalescence changes on released NICs

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: The RSS disable/restore path is scoped only to the newly supplied allowlist at `pkg/daemon/rss_indirection.go:149-158`:

```go
149 func applyRSSIndirection(enabled bool, workers int, allowed []string, execer rssExecutor) {
150     if !enabled {
151         // Kill switch. Actively restore default (equal-weight) RSS on
152         // every allowlisted mlx5 interface so toggling disable at
153         // runtime reverts the table without a daemon restart.
154         // Idempotent: restoring an already-default table is a no-op
155         // ethtool call. The restore is scoped per-interface with the
156         // same driver filter as the apply path, so non-mlx5 netdevs
157         // and non-userspace-dp interfaces are never touched.
158         restoreDefaultRSSIndirection(allowed, execer)
```

Normal application also walks only that current set (`pkg/daemon/rss_indirection.go:192-201`):

```go
192 for _, iface := range allowed {
193     if iface == "lo" {
194         continue
195     }
196     drv := execer.readDriver(iface)
197     if drv != mlx5Driver {
198         // Allowlist can legitimately include non-mlx5 interfaces
199         // (virtio/iavf/i40e that userspace-dp binds on); skip
200         // silently at the driver guard. Codex H1: never invoke
201         // ethtool on a non-mlx5 netdev.
```

Coalescence applies to the same current list (`pkg/daemon/host_tunables_daemon.go:117-126`) and captured original values are restored only at shutdown (`host_tunables_daemon.go:272-280`):

```go
272 if active {
273     restoreHostScopeTunables(prior, realHostTunableFS{})
274 }
275 // Coalescence restore always runs when captures exist.
276 for iface, s := range prior.mlx5Adaptive {
277     restoreMlx5Coalesce(iface, s, realRSSExecutor{})
278 }
279 // #1636: neigh retrans_time_ms restore runs unconditionally (the
280 // apply was never gated on claim-host-tunables) so a co-tenant's
```

The narrow apply caller computes `rssAllowed = UserspaceBoundLinuxInterfaces(cfg)` from only the new config (`daemon_apply_tail.go:292-314`); no prior allowlist is retained.

Trace: (1) An apply binds mlx5 interfaces `{A,B}` to userspace and concentrates RSS/disables adaptive coalescence on both, capturing coalescence originals. (2) A later commit removes B from zones/bindings or disables userspace dataplane, producing current allowlist `{A}` or empty. (3) RSS apply/disable and coalescence iterate only that new set. (4) B remains concentrated and/or adaptive-off with pinned usecs even though xpf no longer owns it. (5) A host workload or another dataplane reusing B sees degraded queue/interrupt behavior until daemon shutdown or manual ethtool repair.

Refutation attempt: I checked worker-count transitions, kill-switch tests, host-scope claim restoration, coalescence capture, userspace-disable behavior, and shutdown ordering. Workers-to-one/queues and explicit RSS disable restore supplied interfaces. Neighbor and host-scope fields retain per-field restore debt. No state records the prior RSS-owned set, and `mlx5Adaptive` is not reconciled against removed names during apply. Tests cover current allowlist scoping and shutdown, not `{A,B}->{A}`.

HPC/invariant check: The tuning is performance-sensitive but runs on the control path. The ownership invariant is that every host/NIC mutation must be restored when an interface leaves xpf ownership, not only when the whole process exits; failed restoration must retain per-interface debt.

Why it matters: A NIC returned to host or another workload can remain artificially limited to old AF_XDP queues and low fixed coalescence, causing throughput loss, interrupt amplification, and surprising cross-workload interference.

Fix direction: Track the last successfully touched RSS interface set and use the coalescence capture map as explicit ownership. On each reconcile, process `old union new`: restore default RSS and captured coalescence for `old-new`, retain failures, then drop ownership only after success. Handle userspace-dataplane disable as withdrawal of the full prior set. Add allowlist-shrink, disable, interface-disappearance, and failed-restore retry tests.

Labels: bug, performance, ethtool, rss, coalescence, lifecycle, resource-ownership

### F9

Title: Failed host-inbound conntrack revocation has no retry trigger

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: The code explicitly allows old authorization to survive a flush failure at `pkg/daemon/host_inbound_conntrack_flush.go:272-280`:

```go
272 // Best effort: the nft host-inbound table is already applied, so enforcement for
273 // NEW connections holds regardless. A conntrack flush failure only leaves
274 // PRE-EXISTING flows on their old authorization (the pre-fix behavior), so it is
275 // logged rather than surfaced as a commit failure — failing the commit would roll
276 // back correct enforcement over a transient conntrack-subsystem error.
277 func (d *Daemon) flushDeniedHostInboundConntrack(views []dpuserspace.ZoneHostInboundView, unzonedV4, unzonedV6 []string, wgListenPorts []uint16) {
278     filter := buildHostInboundConntrackFlushFilter(views, unzonedV4, unzonedV6, wgListenPorts)
279     if filter == nil {
280         return
```

Each family error is only logged and discarded at `pkg/daemon/host_inbound_conntrack_flush.go:282-288`:

```go
282 var flushed uint
283 for _, family := range []netlink.InetFamily{unix.AF_INET, unix.AF_INET6} {
284     n, err := conntrackDeleteFilters(family, filter)
285     if err != nil {
286         slog.Warn("host-inbound conntrack reconcile failed: existing direct-kernel connections to a now-denied host service may retain OLD authorization until they close or time out",
287             "family", family, "err", err)
288         continue
```

The function is invoked after host-inbound apply, not from a background debt worker; the #5566 tests cover matching and successful tightening only.

Trace: (1) A commit removes SSH/HTTPS/other host-inbound admission. (2) nft rules converge, blocking new flows. (3) netlink conntrack deletion fails for IPv4 or IPv6. (4) the established/related accept rule continues to admit already tracked sessions under old authorization. (5) the error is forgotten. (6) With no later config apply, a long-lived keepalive session can remain authorized indefinitely relative to control-plane convergence.

Refutation attempt: I checked per-family independence, filter construction, call sites, commit rollback rationale, and #5566 coverage. Rolling back the newly restrictive nft table would be worse, so failure should remain non-fatal. A later unrelated apply may retry, but no timer, dirty bit, or bounded worker guarantees one. The two families are independent, so one successful family does not repair the other.

HPC/invariant check: This runs after apply and does not touch the userspace packet hot path. The authorization invariant is that session revocation debt must be retried until acknowledged without rolling back stricter new-connection enforcement.

Why it matters: An administrator who removes a host service can leave an existing direct-kernel management session authorized after the commit, defeating the intended immediate revocation semantics established by #5566.

Fix direction: Record a per-family dirty filter/generation on failure and retry asynchronously with bounded backoff until success or a newer policy supersedes it. Keep commit success for the nft restriction, expose debt in status/metrics, and test fail-then-retry plus generation replacement.

### F10

Title: Unexpected management listener death is observable but never reconciled at the same endpoint

Severity: Medium

Confidence: High

Gate verdict: MATERIAL

Evidence: Reconcile exits only for a nil server and otherwise compares desired endpoint fingerprints, not liveness (`pkg/daemon/management.go:197-204`):

```go
197 func (m *managementReconciler) reconcileTo(next api.Config) error {
198     m.mu.Lock()
199     defer m.mu.Unlock()
200     if m.srv == nil {
201         // API disabled (--api-addr empty) or a boot bind never succeeded: nothing
202         // live to reconcile.
203         return nil
204     }
```

An unchanged dead HTTP endpoint therefore skips `ReconcileHTTP` at `pkg/daemon/management.go:208-217`:

```go
208 // HTTP leg: make-before-break rebind ONLY if the HTTP bind changed. Advance
209 // the converged fingerprint only on success (retry debt on failure); httpOK
210 // records whether the live HTTP listener is now at next.Addr.
211 httpOK := true
212 if next.Addr != m.cur.addr {
213     if err := m.srv.ReconcileHTTP(next.Addr); err != nil {
214         errs = append(errs, err)
215         httpOK = false
216     } else {
217         m.cur.addr = next.Addr
```

Even a direct same-address call is a no-op based on configured address, not `dead`, at `pkg/api/listener.go:175-183`:

```go
175 func (s *Server) ReconcileHTTP(addr string) error {
176     s.lifeMu.Lock()
177     defer s.lifeMu.Unlock()
178     if addr == "" {
179         return fmt.Errorf("api: refusing to reconcile the HTTP listener to an empty bind address")
180     }
181     if s.httpLeg != nil && s.httpLeg.srv.Addr == addr {
182         return nil
183     }
```

`effectiveHTTPListener` correctly reports the dead leg as failed (`management.go:151-180`), and the assigned #6401 test verifies only that diagnostic.

Trace: (1) HTTP starts and `curSet`/`m.srv` are populated. (2) `http.Server.Serve` exits unexpectedly; `listenerLeg.dead` becomes true and status reports `Failed`. (3) Desired config remains at the same address. (4) Every ordinary management reconcile sees `next.Addr == m.cur.addr` and takes no listener action. (5) Even a direct same-address API reconcile returns before checking `dead`. (6) REST management stays unavailable until an endpoint-changing commit or daemon restart.

Refutation attempt: I checked serve-goroutine exit handling, effective status, same-address API behavior, management apply call sites, make-before-break semantics, and GH#6721. No supervisor treats an unexpected HTTP leg exit as daemon-fatal or restarts it. HTTPS uses analogous fingerprint gating. GH#6721 is the boot case where `m.srv` stays nil; here the server and converged fingerprint exist, so fixing only boot retry does not repair dead-leg restart.

HPC/invariant check: Listener lifecycle is off the packet path. Locking is internally race-safe; the violated lifecycle invariant is that a desired enabled service in `Failed` state must create retry debt independent of whether its configuration fingerprint changed.

Why it matters: A transient listener failure causes a permanent REST management outage with a clear failed status but no self-healing action.

Fix direction: Make `ReconcileHTTP`/`ReconcileHTTPS` liveness-aware: same address is a no-op only when the leg exists and is not dead. Have management reconcile invoke the leg when effective state is failed, and trigger an immediate bounded retry/supervisor on unexpected serve exit. Add a test that kills a leg, reconciles unchanged config, and proves a new listener serves before the dead leg is retired.

Labels: bug, daemon-lifecycle, api, system-services, self-healing

### C1a

Title: Runtime hostname success can mask a failed durable hostname write

Severity: Low

Confidence: High

Evidence: `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:394-402` returns solely on runtime equality:

```go
394 current, _ := os.Hostname()
395 if current == cfg.System.HostName {
396     return
397 }
398
399 if err := syscall.Sethostname([]byte(cfg.System.HostName)); err != nil {
400     slog.Warn("failed to set hostname", "err", err)
401     return
402 }
```

The durable write failure is then only logged at `pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:404-408`:

```go
404 // Persist to /etc/hostname (DurableState: node identity must survive
405 // a power cut so the box keeps its configured name across reboot).
406 if err := fsatomic.WriteFileDurable("/etc/hostname", []byte(cfg.System.HostName+"\n"), 0644); err != nil {
407     slog.Warn("failed to write /etc/hostname", "err", err)
408 }
```

Trace: Runtime `sethostname` succeeds, the durable write fails, and unchanged applies return at line 396. A reboot normally re-drives the config after initially loading the old file, so the discrepancy is bounded to early boot or a later xpfd startup failure.

Refutation attempt: Reboot apply usually repairs the file, which materially limits impact. There is still no same-boot retry or status signal, and the code's own durability comment is not met after a failed write.

HPC/invariant check: No hot-path concern; this is a small durable-state acknowledgement gap.

Why it matters: Early-boot services can observe the old hostname after power loss, and the configured identity depends on xpfd reaching this apply step again.

Fix direction: Compare/reconcile `/etc/hostname` independently of the runtime value, return or retain durable-write debt, and test runtime-match/file-mismatch repair.

Labels: cohort, hostname, durability, cold-boot

### C1b

Title: Sequential per-NIC ethtool timeouts have no aggregate apply budget

Severity: Low

Confidence: Medium

Gate verdict: COHORT

Evidence: Each command can consume 15 seconds plus a 5-second pipe-drain delay at `pkg/daemon/exec_timeout.go:43-49`:

```go
43 // WaitDelay caps the post-SIGKILL pipe-drain window. Without it,
44 // CombinedOutput blocks until all write-end holders (e.g. PAM exec
45 // helpers spawned by useradd) close their copies of the pipe — which
46 // may be long after the main process is killed. 5s is generous for
47 // simple admin commands; the hard ceiling becomes 15s+5s=20s per site.
48 cmd.WaitDelay = 5 * time.Second
49 return cmd.CombinedOutput()
```

RSS walks every allowed interface serially at `pkg/daemon/rss_indirection.go:192-201`, with probe/write calls inside `applyRSSIndirectionOne`; coalescence repeats a serial probe/write walk through the same executor. The caller runs this in the serialized apply tail.

Trace: On a multi-NIC host, slow or wedged ethtool operations consume their individual bound one after another while `applySem` remains occupied; total commit/HA-sync latency scales with interface count and operations per interface.

Refutation attempt: #1794 ensures no single command is unbounded, and typical appliances have few mlx5 interfaces. That keeps this below individual materiality, but it does not cap aggregate latency for larger hosts or repeated slow ioctl failures.

HPC/invariant check: The work is intentionally off the packet path, but holding the global apply serializer creates control-plane head-of-line blocking.

Why it matters: A degraded NIC/driver can turn an otherwise small commit into a long management and HA-sync stall proportional to configured interfaces.

Fix direction: Thread an apply-phase context with an aggregate deadline through the executor, stop launching new best-effort probes after expiry, retain skipped-interface debt, and consider bounded per-interface concurrency only after validating driver safety.

Labels: cohort, performance, latency, ethtool, apply

Dedup note: Closed #1794 bounded individual commands; no current issue covers the aggregate sequential RSS/coalescence phase.
